Algebra, Percentages & Proportions.q: It takes 3 aides 8 hours to restock all of a hospital's supply rooms. Working at the same rate, how long would it take 4 aides to do the same job?
o: 10 hours 40 minutes
2 hours
7 hours
6 hours
Algebra, Percentages & Proportions.w: This is an inverse proportion: aides × hours stays constant. 3 × 8 = 24 aide-hours, so 4 aides need 24 ÷ 4 = 6 hours.

n.0: This treats the relationship as direct. More aides finish faster, so the time must decrease.
n.1: This divides the original 8 hours by 4 aides and ignores that the 8 hours was for 3 aides.
n.2: This subtracts 1 hour for the 1 extra aide. The total work, 24 aide-hours, stays the same.

Algebra, Percentages & Proportions.q: Solve the proportion (x + 2)/9 = 4/6.
Algebra, Percentages & Proportions.w: Cross-multiply: 6(x + 2) = 4 × 9 = 36. Divide by 6: x + 2 = 6. Subtract 2: x = 4. Check: 6/9 = 2/3 and 4/6 = 2/3.

n.0: This flips the second ratio, solving (x + 2)/9 = 6/4.
n.1: This cross-multiplies without distributing: 6x + 2 = 36 instead of 6(x + 2) = 36.
n.2: This uses addition: 9 is 3 more than 6, so it adds 3 to 4. Proportions scale by multiplying.

Algebra, Percentages & Proportions.q: A survey at a health fair found that 7 of every 20 visitors had their blood pressure checked. If 1,260 people visited the fair, how many would be expected to have had their blood pressure checked?
Algebra, Percentages & Proportions.w: Set up 7/20 = x/1,260. Cross-multiply: 20x = 8,820, so x = 441.

n.0: This divides 1,260 by 7 instead of multiplying by 7/20.
n.1: This is 1/20 of the visitors, the size of one part, not 7 parts.
n.2: This is the number expected not to have had a check (13 of every 20).

Algebra, Percentages & Proportions.q: A printer in a clinic prints 18 pages in 45 seconds. At this rate, how many pages can it print in 4 minutes?
Algebra, Percentages & Proportions.w: Convert first: 4 minutes = 240 seconds. Set up 18/45 = p/240. Cross-multiply: 45p = 4,320, so p = 96 pages.

n.0: This treats 18 pages as the number printed per minute, multiplying 18 by 4.
n.1: This divides 45 by 18 and multiplies by 4, which inverts the rate.
n.3: This mixes units, comparing 4 minutes with 45 seconds without converting 4 minutes to 240 seconds.

Algebra, Percentages & Proportions.q: Nine gallons of gas cost $31.41. Which proportion can be used to find c, the cost of 14 gallons of gas at the same price per gallon?
Algebra, Percentages & Proportions.w: Keep the same units in the same positions: 9 gallons/$31.41 = 14 gallons/c. Cross-multiplying gives 9c = 439.74, so c = $48.86.

n.0: This puts the second ratio upside down. Gallons over dollars must be matched with gallons over dollars.
n.1: This pairs $31.41 with 14 gallons, but $31.41 is the cost of 9 gallons.
n.2: This pairs 9 gallons with the unknown cost and 14 gallons with $31.41, mismatching the quantities.

Algebra, Percentages & Proportions.q: A 12-ounce bag of coffee makes 45 cups. At the same rate, how many cups can be made from a 32-ounce bag? Enter the number of cups.

tr.65: Added the 20-ounce difference to 45 instead of scaling.
tr.8.53: Set up the second ratio upside down (12 × 32 ÷ 45).

Algebra, Percentages & Proportions.w: Set up 12/45 = 32/c. Cross-multiply: 12c = 1,440, so c = 120 cups.

Algebra, Percentages & Proportions.q: A patient-education poster is enlarged proportionally from a draft that is 8 inches wide and 10 inches tall. The poster is 26 inches wide. How tall is the poster? Enter the number of inches.

tr.28: Added the 18-inch increase in width to the height instead of scaling.
tr.20.8: Set up the ratio upside down (26 × 8 ÷ 10).

Algebra, Percentages & Proportions.w: Set up width/height: 8/10 = 26/h. Cross-multiply: 8h = 260, so h = 32.5 inches.

Algebra, Percentages & Proportions.q: Two rectangular rooms are similar. The smaller room is 10 feet by 12 feet, and its 10-foot side corresponds to a 15-foot side of the larger room. What is the area of the larger room?
o: 405 square feet
180 square feet
255 square feet
270 square feet
Algebra, Percentages & Proportions.w: Scale factor = 15 ÷ 10 = 1.5. The other side: 12 × 1.5 = 18 feet. Area = 15 × 18 = 270 square feet (equivalently, 120 × 2.25 = 270).

n.0: This multiplies the area by 1.5³ = 3.375, the factor for volume, not area.
n.1: This multiplies the smaller room's 120-square-foot area by the linear scale factor 1.5. Areas scale by 1.5² = 2.25.
n.2: This adds 5 feet to the 12-foot side instead of multiplying it by 1.5, giving 15 × 17.

Algebra, Percentages & Proportions.q: Which pair of quantities is in an inverse proportion?
o: The miles driven and the gallons of gas used at a steady fuel economy
The hours worked and the pay earned at a fixed hourly wage
The number of nurses sharing a fixed workload and the hours it takes
The number of 250 mg tablets given and the total milligrams given
Algebra, Percentages & Proportions.w: In an inverse proportion the product stays constant: doubling the number of nurses on a fixed workload halves the hours. The other pairs increase together (direct proportion).

n.0: Miles and gallons increase together at a constant rate, so this is a direct proportion.
n.1: Pay grows at a constant rate as hours increase, so this is a direct proportion.
n.3: Each extra tablet adds 250 mg, so the total grows with the count: a direct proportion.

Algebra, Percentages & Proportions.q: A provider orders amoxicillin 375 mg by mouth. The pharmacy supplies amoxicillin oral suspension containing 250 mg per 5 mL. How many milliliters should be given?
o: 7.5 mL
3.3 mL
75 mL
1.5 mL
Algebra, Percentages & Proportions.w: Desired ÷ have × quantity: 375 ÷ 250 × 5 = 1.5 × 5 = 7.5 mL. As a proportion: 250 mg/5 mL = 375 mg/x, so 250x = 1,875 and x = 7.5 mL.

n.1: This inverts the dose ratio, using 250/375 × 5 instead of 375/250 × 5.
n.2: This divides 375 mg by 5 mL, as if each milliliter held 5 mg.
n.3: This divides the desired dose by the dose on hand but does not multiply by the 5 mL quantity.

Algebra, Percentages & Proportions.q: A soup recipe that serves 6 people uses 2 1/4 cups of broth. How many cups of broth are needed to make the recipe serve 10 people?
o: 6 1/4 cups
3 3/4 cups
4 1/2 cups
1 7/20 cups
Algebra, Percentages & Proportions.w: Set up 2.25/6 = x/10. Cross-multiply: 6x = 22.5, so x = 3.75 = 3 3/4 cups.

n.0: This adds 4 cups for the 4 extra servings instead of scaling by 10/6.
n.2: This doubles the recipe, but 10 servings is 10/6 = 1 2/3 times the recipe, not 2 times.
n.3: This sets up the proportion upside down, multiplying 2 1/4 by 6/10.

Algebra, Percentages & Proportions.q: On a floor plan, 1/4 inch represents 1 foot. A rectangular nurses' station measures 3 3/4 inches by 2 1/2 inches on the plan. What is the actual area of the nurses' station?
o: 37.5 square feet
50 square feet
150 square feet
9.375 square feet
Algebra, Percentages & Proportions.w: 1 inch represents 4 feet. Length: 3.75 × 4 = 15 feet. Width: 2.5 × 4 = 10 feet. Area: 15 × 10 = 150 square feet.

n.0: This multiplies the plan area by the linear factor 4. Each dimension is multiplied by 4, so the area is multiplied by 16.
n.1: This is the perimeter of the 15-foot by 10-foot station, 2(15 + 10), not its area.
n.3: This is the area measured on the plan, 3.75 × 2.5, without converting to actual feet.

Algebra, Percentages & Proportions.q: A medication is ordered at 15 mg per kilogram of body weight per day, divided into 3 equal doses. A child weighs 44 pounds. Using 1 kg = 2.2 lb, how many milligrams should be given in each dose?
o: 300 mg
100 mg
660 mg
220 mg
Algebra, Percentages & Proportions.w: Weight: 44 ÷ 2.2 = 20 kg. Daily dose: 15 × 20 = 300 mg. Each dose: 300 ÷ 3 = 100 mg.

n.0: This is the total daily dose; it must be divided into 3 equal doses.
n.2: This uses the weight in pounds and also gives a daily total, 44 × 15.
n.3: This uses the weight in pounds (44 × 15 ÷ 3) instead of converting to 20 kg first.

Algebra, Percentages & Proportions.q: On a state map, 1.5 inches represents 40 miles. Two towns are 5.25 inches apart on the map. What is the actual distance between the two towns?
o: 141.75 miles
210 miles
315 miles
140 miles
Algebra, Percentages & Proportions.w: Set up 1.5/40 = 5.25/d. Cross-multiply: 1.5d = 210, so d = 140 miles.

n.0: This rounds 26.67 miles per inch to 27 before multiplying. Round only at the end.
n.1: This multiplies 5.25 by 40 as if 1 inch represented 40 miles.
n.2: This multiplies 40 by 1.5 to get 60 miles per inch instead of dividing.

Algebra, Percentages & Proportions.q: A cleaning solution for patient rooms is mixed using 3 ounces of concentrate for every 2 gallons of water. How many ounces of concentrate are needed for 4.5 gallons of water?
o: 6.75 ounces
13.5 ounces
5.5 ounces
3 ounces
Algebra, Percentages & Proportions.w: Set up 3/2 = x/4.5. Cross-multiply: 2x = 13.5, so x = 6.75 ounces.

n.1: This multiplies 3 ounces by 4.5 as if the 3 ounces were for 1 gallon.
n.2: This adds the extra 2.5 gallons to the 3 ounces instead of scaling.
n.3: This sets up the proportion upside down, multiplying 4.5 by 2/3.

Algebra, Percentages & Proportions.q: A pancake recipe uses 1 1/2 cups of flour and 3/4 cup of milk. Kim has 2 cups of milk and wants to use all of it, keeping the same ratio of flour to milk. How many cups of flour does she need?
o: 1 cup
4 cups
3 cups
2 3/4 cups
Algebra, Percentages & Proportions.w: Flour/milk: 1.5/0.75 = x/2. The recipe uses 2 cups of flour per cup of milk (1.5 ÷ 0.75 = 2), so 2 × 2 = 4 cups of flour.

n.0: This sets up the ratio upside down, multiplying 2 by 3/4 and dividing by 1 1/2.
n.2: This multiplies 2 by 1 1/2 as if the 1 1/2 cups of flour went with 1 cup of milk.
n.3: This adds the extra 1 1/4 cups of milk to the flour instead of scaling.

Algebra, Percentages & Proportions.q: An architect builds a model of a new hospital wing at a scale of 1:200. The model is 45 centimeters tall. How tall will the actual building be, in meters? (1 meter = 100 centimeters)
o: 0.225 meters
90 meters
9 meters
900 meters
Algebra, Percentages & Proportions.w: Each model centimeter represents 200 actual centimeters: 45 × 200 = 9,000 cm. Convert: 9,000 ÷ 100 = 90 meters.

n.0: This divides the model height by 200 instead of multiplying; the real building is larger than the model.
n.2: This divides 9,000 cm by 1,000 instead of 100; there are 100 cm in a meter.
n.3: This divides 9,000 cm by 10 instead of 100; there are 100 cm in a meter.

Algebra, Percentages & Proportions.q: A provider orders heparin 7,500 units. The vial is labeled 5,000 units per mL. How many milliliters should be drawn up? Enter the number of milliliters.
Algebra, Percentages & Proportions.w: Desired ÷ have × quantity: 7,500 ÷ 5,000 × 1 mL = 1.5 mL. As a proportion: 5,000 units/1 mL = 7,500 units/x, so x = 1.5 mL.

Algebra, Percentages & Proportions.q: A punch recipe mixes 3 cups of juice with 5 cups of sparkling water. How many cups of juice are needed to make 14 cups of punch? Enter the number of cups.

tr.8.4: Used the part-to-part ratio 3/5 as the fraction of the punch that is juice.
tr.8.75: Found the amount of sparkling water instead of juice.

Algebra, Percentages & Proportions.w: The recipe makes 3 + 5 = 8 cups, and 3 of those 8 cups are juice. Juice = 3/8 × 14 = 5.25 cups.

Algebra, Percentages & Proportions.q: The scale on a trail map is 2 centimeters to 0.5 kilometer. A hike measures 13 centimeters on the map. What is the actual length of the hike?
o: 3.25 kilometers
26 kilometers
52 kilometers
6.5 kilometers
Algebra, Percentages & Proportions.w: Set up 2/0.5 = 13/d. Cross-multiply: 2d = 6.5, so d = 3.25 kilometers. (1 cm represents 0.25 km, and 13 × 0.25 = 3.25.)

n.1: This multiplies 13 by 2 and leaves out the 0.5 km.
n.2: This sets up the proportion upside down, multiplying 13 by 2 ÷ 0.5.
n.3: This multiplies 13 by 0.5 as if 1 cm represented 0.5 km; it is 2 cm that represents 0.5 km.

Algebra, Percentages & Proportions.q: A provider orders 60 mg of a liquid medication every 6 hours. The medication is supplied as 20 mg per 5 mL. How many milliliters will the patient receive in 24 hours?
o: 75 mL
15 mL
60 mL
360 mL
Algebra, Percentages & Proportions.w: One dose: 60 ÷ 20 × 5 = 15 mL. Doses in 24 hours: 24 ÷ 6 = 4. Total: 4 × 15 = 60 mL.

n.0: This counts 5 doses by including both hour 0 and hour 24; every 6 hours gives 4 doses in a 24-hour day.
n.1: This is the volume for one dose; there are 24 ÷ 6 = 4 doses in 24 hours.
n.3: This multiplies one 15 mL dose by 24 as if a dose were given every hour.

Algebra, Percentages & Proportions.q: A patient has a fluid allowance of 1,200 mL for the day. She uses 1/4 of the allowance at breakfast, and then 2/3 of the remaining amount over lunch and dinner. How many milliliters are left for the evening?
o: 900 mL
300 mL
600 mL
100 mL
Algebra, Percentages & Proportions.w: Breakfast: 1/4 × 1,200 = 300 mL, leaving 900 mL. Lunch and dinner: 2/3 × 900 = 600 mL, leaving 900 - 600 = 300 mL for the evening.

n.0: This is the amount left after breakfast, an intermediate step; lunch and dinner still have to be subtracted.
n.2: This is the amount used at lunch and dinner, not the amount left.
n.3: This takes 2/3 of the full 1,200 mL instead of 2/3 of the 900 mL remaining after breakfast.

Algebra, Percentages & Proportions.q: Plan A costs $45 per month plus $0.05 per text message. Plan B costs $30 per month plus $0.10 per text message. For what number of texts in a month do the two plans cost the same?
Algebra, Percentages & Proportions.w: Set the costs equal: 45 + 0.05t = 30 + 0.10t. Subtract 0.05t and 30: 15 = 0.05t, so t = 300 texts. Check: 45 + 15 = $60 and 30 + 30 = $60.

n.1: This adds the per-text rates (0.15) instead of subtracting them.
n.2: This adds the monthly charges ($75) instead of subtracting them.
n.3: This divides the $15 difference by Plan B's rate alone instead of by the 0.05 difference in rates.

Algebra, Percentages & Proportions.q: Malik earns $17.50 per hour and worked 32 hours this week. 15% of his gross pay is withheld for taxes. From his take-home pay he pays $210 toward rent and $95 for groceries. How much of his take-home pay is left?

n.0: This subtracts the bills first and then takes 15% from what is left. Taxes are withheld from the full $560.
n.2: This is the take-home pay, an intermediate step; rent and groceries still have to be subtracted.
n.3: This subtracts rent and groceries from the gross pay of $560 and leaves out the 15% withheld for taxes.

Algebra, Percentages & Proportions.q: Three patients are in consecutive even-numbered rooms. The sum of the three room numbers is 642. What is the lowest of the three room numbers?
Algebra, Percentages & Proportions.w: Let the rooms be n, n + 2, and n + 4. Then 3n + 6 = 642, so 3n = 636 and n = 212. Check: 212 + 214 + 216 = 642.

n.0: This is the middle room number (642 ÷ 3), not the lowest.
n.1: This is the highest of the three room numbers.
n.2: This uses consecutive integers (n, n + 1, n + 2), giving 3n + 3 = 642. Consecutive even numbers differ by 2.

Algebra, Percentages & Proportions.q: A nurse begins a 12.5-hour shift at 6:45 p.m. She stays 40 minutes after the shift ends to finish charting. At what time does she leave?
Algebra, Percentages & Proportions.w: 12.5 hours = 12 hours 30 minutes. 6:45 p.m. + 12 hours = 6:45 a.m.; + 30 minutes = 7:15 a.m. (end of shift); + 40 minutes = 7:55 a.m.

n.1: This reads 12.5 hours as 12 hours 50 minutes; 0.5 hour is 30 minutes.
n.2: Twelve and a half hours after 6:45 p.m. is the next morning, so the time is a.m.
n.3: This is when the shift ends; the 40 minutes of charting must be added.

Algebra, Percentages & Proportions.q: Jada and Luis split $1,260 in tutoring income. Jada receives $180 more than twice Luis's share. How much does Luis receive?
Algebra, Percentages & Proportions.w: Let L = Luis's share, so Jada's is 2L + 180. Then L + 2L + 180 = 1,260, so 3L = 1,080 and L = $360. Jada gets 2(360) + 180 = $900; 360 + 900 = 1,260.

n.0: This is Jada's share, not Luis's.
n.1: This adds the $180 to $1,260 instead of subtracting it, giving 3L = 1,440.
n.3: This divides $1,080 by 2 instead of by 3. Luis's share counts once and Jada's contains it twice, so there are 3 shares.

Algebra, Percentages & Proportions.q: A bottle holds 250 mL of a liquid medication. The prescribed dose is 7.5 mL twice a day. How many full days will the bottle last?
o: 17 days
33 days
34 days
16 days
Algebra, Percentages & Proportions.w: Daily use: 7.5 × 2 = 15 mL. Days: 250 ÷ 15 = 16.67. Only complete days count, so round down to 16 days (16 × 15 = 240 mL).

n.0: This rounds 16.67 up. After 16 days only 10 mL is left, which is not enough for both doses on day 17.
n.1: This is the number of full doses (250 ÷ 7.5), not days; there are 2 doses per day.
n.2: This rounds the number of doses (33.3) up and treats each dose as a day.

Algebra, Percentages & Proportions.q: A caterer charges a $150 setup fee plus $18.50 per guest for a nursing school graduation party. Which statements about the cost are true? Select all that apply.
o: A budget of $1,000 covers at most 46 guests.
Doubling the guests from 40 to 80 doubles the total cost.
A bill of $1,075 corresponds to 50 guests.
The cost for 40 guests is $890.
The cost for 60 guests is $1,110.

n.0: (1,000 - 150) ÷ 18.50 = 45.9, so the budget covers at most 45 guests; 46 guests would cost $1,001.
n.1: 80 guests cost 150 + 1,480 = $1,630, not 2 × 890 = $1,780. The $150 fee is charged once, so the cost is not directly proportional to the number of guests.
n.4: 18.50 × 60 = $1,110 leaves out the $150 setup fee; the total is $1,260.

Algebra, Percentages & Proportions.q: A clinic can buy exam gloves in a box of 100 for $8.40 or in a case of 10 such boxes for $76.50. How much is saved per glove by buying the case instead of single boxes?
o: 0.75 cent
0.075 cent
75 cents
7.5 cents
Algebra, Percentages & Proportions.w: Single box: $8.40 ÷ 100 = $0.084 per glove. Case: $76.50 ÷ 1,000 = $0.0765 per glove. Savings: 0.084 - 0.0765 = $0.0075 per glove, which is 0.75 cent.

n.1: Decimal slip: $0.0075 is 0.75 cent; this moves the decimal one place too far.
n.2: This is the savings per box of 100 gloves ($8.40 - $7.65), not per glove.
n.3: Decimal slip: $0.0075 is 0.75 of a cent, not 7.5 cents.

Algebra, Percentages & Proportions.q: Sam's gym membership costs $35 per month, and a personal trainer charges $45 per session. Sam budgets no more than $400 per month for the gym and training combined. What is the greatest number of training sessions he can book in a month? Enter a whole number.

tr.9: Rounded up; 9 sessions plus the membership cost $440, which is over budget.

Algebra, Percentages & Proportions.w: Write 35 + 45s ≤ 400. Subtract 35: 45s ≤ 365. Divide by 45: s ≤ 8.11. The greatest whole number is 8 (35 + 360 = $395).

Algebra, Percentages & Proportions.q: A clinic orders 3 cases of syringes at $42.75 per case and 5 boxes of alcohol pads at $6.90 per box. A 20% discount applies to the supplies, and then a $12.45 shipping charge is added without a discount. What is the total cost of the order? Enter the amount in dollars, to the nearest cent.

tr.175.2: Added the shipping without applying the discount.
tr.140.16: Applied the 20% discount to the shipping charge as well.

Algebra, Percentages & Proportions.q: A tutoring center charges $25 per session for the first 4 sessions and $20 for each session after that. Which expression gives the total cost, in dollars, of n sessions when n is greater than 4?

n.0: This charges for the sessions after the fourth and leaves out the $100 for the first 4.
n.1: This adds $100 for the first 4 sessions but also charges $20 for those same 4 sessions; the $20 rate applies to n - 4 sessions.
n.2: This charges $25 for every session and then charges again for the sessions after the fourth.

Measurement & Geometry.q: A bottle contains 0.6 liter of sterile saline. A nurse pours out 3 doses of 85 milliliters each for wound care. How many milliliters of saline remain in the bottle? Enter your answer in milliliters.

tr.515: Subtracted one 85 mL dose instead of all three.
tr.5745: Converted 0.6 L to 6,000 mL (four places) before subtracting 255 mL.

Measurement & Geometry.w: Convert the bottle to milliliters: 0.6 L × 1,000 = 600 mL. Amount poured = 3 × 85 = 255 mL. Remaining = 600 - 255 = 345 mL.

Measurement & Geometry.q: A child who weighs 18 kilograms is prescribed a medication at 15 milligrams per kilogram per day, divided into 3 equal doses. How many grams of the medication are in each dose? Enter your answer in grams.

tr.90: Stopped at milligrams; the question asks for grams.
tr.0.27: Gave the full daily amount (270 mg = 0.27 g) instead of one of the 3 doses.

Measurement & Geometry.w: Daily amount = 15 mg × 18 = 270 mg. Each dose = 270 ÷ 3 = 90 mg. Milligrams to grams: divide by 1,000, so 90 mg = 0.09 g.

Measurement & Geometry.q: A pharmacy technician is sorting five powder samples by mass. The labels use different metric units. Place the samples in order from least mass to greatest mass, starting with the least.
o: 380 mg

Measurement & Geometry.q: A lab technician has 2.5 liters of a buffer solution. Each test tube must be filled with exactly 15 milliliters of the solution. How many test tubes can be completely filled from the 2.5 liters?
Measurement & Geometry.w: 2.5 L × 1,000 = 2,500 mL. 2,500 ÷ 15 = 166.67. Only complete tubes count, so round down to 166.

n.0: 2,500 ÷ 15 = 166.67, but the 167th tube cannot be completely filled, so round down.
n.1: This treats 2.5 L as 25,000 mL (multiplying by 10,000); 1 L = 1,000 mL.
n.3: This treats 2.5 L as 250 mL (multiplying by 100); 1 L = 1,000 mL.

Measurement & Geometry.q: A wound measured 3.4 centimeters long when it was assessed on Monday. On Friday, the same wound measured 27 millimeters long. By how many millimeters did the length of the wound decrease?
o: 7 mm
0.7 mm
313 mm
Measurement & Geometry.w: 3.4 cm × 10 = 34 mm. Decrease = 34 - 27 = 7 mm.

n.1: This subtracts 3.4 from 27 without first converting 3.4 cm to millimeters.
n.2: 0.7 is the decrease in centimeters; 0.7 cm = 7 mm.
n.3: This converts 3.4 cm to 340 mm by multiplying by 100; 1 cm = 10 mm.

Measurement & Geometry.q: A nutrition study records each participant's fluid intake in deciliters. One participant drank 1.8 liters of water during the day. How many deciliters should the researcher record for this participant?
o: 180 dL
18 dL
Measurement & Geometry.w: Deci- means one tenth, so 1 L = 10 dL. 1.8 × 10 = 18 dL.

n.0: This uses 100 per liter, which is the centiliter factor (1 L = 100 cL).
n.1: This uses 1,000 per liter, which is the milliliter factor (1 L = 1,000 mL).
n.3: This divides by 10. A deciliter is smaller than a liter, so the number of deciliters must be larger.

Measurement & Geometry.q: Four specimen containers are labeled with their capacities: container W holds 0.45 L, container X holds 405 mL, container Y holds 4.6 dL, and container Z holds 44 cL. Which container has the greatest capacity?
o: Container Y
Container X
Container Z
Container W
Measurement & Geometry.w: Convert to milliliters: W = 0.45 × 1,000 = 450 mL; X = 405 mL; Y = 4.6 × 100 = 460 mL; Z = 44 × 10 = 440 mL. Container Y holds the most.

n.1: 405 is the largest number shown, but 405 mL is less than 450 mL and 460 mL.
n.2: 44 cL = 440 mL, which is less than 460 mL.
n.3: 0.45 L = 450 mL, which is less than 4.6 dL = 460 mL.

Measurement & Geometry.q: An IV infusion pump delivers fluid at a constant rate of 125 milliliters per hour. If the rate is not changed, how many liters of fluid will the patient receive during a 12-hour shift?

n.0: This divides 1,500 mL by 100 instead of 1,000.
n.1: This divides 1,500 mL by 10,000 instead of 1,000.
n.3: This is the amount for one hour (125 mL); multiply by the 12 hours first.

Measurement & Geometry.q: A nurse records a newborn's weight as 7 pounds 13 ounces. The nursery's electronic scale displays weight in ounces. What weight, in ounces, should the scale display for this newborn?
o: 83 oz
97 oz
125 oz
112 oz

n.0: This uses 10 ounces per pound, treating pounds like a decimal unit; 1 lb = 16 oz.
n.1: This uses 12 ounces per pound; 1 lb = 16 oz.
n.3: This converts the 7 pounds (7 × 16 = 112 oz) but does not add the 13 ounces.

Measurement & Geometry.q: A roll of medical tape is 5 yards long. A nurse cuts strips that are each 8 inches long to secure dressings. How many complete 8-inch strips can be cut from the roll?
Measurement & Geometry.w: 5 yd × 36 in per yd = 180 in. 180 ÷ 8 = 22.5, so 22 complete strips can be cut.

n.0: This uses 12 inches per yard (5 yd = 60 in); 1 yd = 36 in.
n.1: 180 ÷ 8 = 22.5, and half a strip is not a complete strip, so round down.
n.3: This uses 10 inches per foot (15 ft = 150 in); 1 ft = 12 in.

Measurement & Geometry.q: For a clinic open house, each of 5 tables needs 3 quarts of lemonade. The lemonade is sold in half-gallon jugs. What is the least number of jugs that must be bought to supply all 5 tables?
Measurement & Geometry.w: Total = 5 × 3 = 15 qt. A gallon is 4 qt, so a half gallon is 2 qt. 15 ÷ 2 = 7.5, so round up to 8 jugs.

n.0: This divides by 4 quarts, the amount in a full gallon rather than a half gallon.
n.2: This multiplies 15 quarts by 2 instead of dividing by the 2 quarts in each jug.
n.3: 15 ÷ 2 = 7.5, and 7 jugs hold 14 qt, which is not enough, so round up.

Measurement & Geometry.q: An IV infusion is started at 9:40 a.m. and is programmed to run for 2.6 hours without stopping. At what time will the infusion finish?

n.0: This reads 2.6 hours as 260 minutes (4 h 20 min).
n.1: This reads 2.6 hours as 2 hours 6 minutes; 0.6 h = 0.6 × 60 = 36 min.

Measurement & Geometry.q: A decorative window is shaped like a semicircle with a straight bottom edge 4 feet long. A builder needs trim for the entire edge of the window, including the curved part and the straight bottom. How many feet of trim are needed? Use 3.14 for pi.
Measurement & Geometry.w: Curved part = 1/2 × πd = 1/2 × 3.14 × 4 = 6.28 ft. Add the straight edge (the diameter): 6.28 + 4 = 10.28 ft.

n.0: This adds the 4-foot straight edge to a full circle's circumference instead of half of it.
n.1: This is the circumference of a full circle (3.14 × 4).
n.3: This is the curved part by itself; the 4-foot straight edge must be added.

Measurement & Geometry.q: A circular garden has a circumference of 62.8 feet. The gardener needs its area to buy the right amount of mulch. What is the area of the garden? Use 3.14 for pi. Enter the number of square feet.

tr.100: Stopped at r² = 100 without multiplying by pi.
tr.1256: Used the diameter (20 ft) as the radius.
tr.31.4: Multiplied pi by the radius (3.14 × 10) instead of by the radius squared.

Measurement & Geometry.q: A square patio tabletop is 30 inches on each side. A circular hole with a diameter of 10 inches is cut out of the center for an umbrella pole. What is the area of the tabletop that remains? Use 3.14 for pi. Enter the number of square inches.

tr.586: Used the diameter (10 in) as the radius of the hole (3.14 × 100 = 314).
tr.868.6: Subtracted the hole's circumference (31.4 in) instead of its area.
tr.78.5: Gave the area of the hole instead of the area that remains.

Measurement & Geometry.w: Square = 30 × 30 = 900 in². Hole: r = 5 in, so A = 3.14 × 5² = 78.5 in². Remaining = 900 - 78.5 = 821.5 in².

Measurement & Geometry.q: A circular pizza with a diameter of 14 inches is cut into 8 equal slices. What is the area of one slice, to the nearest tenth of a square inch? Use 3.14 for pi.
o: 76.9 in²
5.5 in²
19.2 in²

n.0: This is the area of the whole pizza; divide it by the 8 slices.
n.1: This uses the diameter (14 in) as the radius.
n.2: This divides the circumference (43.96 in) by 8; the area of a slice comes from πr².

Measurement & Geometry.q: A clinic stocks two sizes of circular wound dressings. The small dressing has a radius of 3 centimeters, and the large dressing has a radius of 6 centimeters. How many more square centimeters does the large dressing cover? Use 3.14 for pi.

n.1: This uses the diameters (6 cm and 12 cm) as the radii.
n.2: This assumes doubling the radius doubles the area; it multiplies the area by 4.
n.3: This is the difference in circumferences (37.68 - 18.84), not in areas.

Measurement & Geometry.q: A lawn sprinkler waters a circular region with an area of 113.04 square meters. A landscaper needs the width of the region measured straight across through its center. What is the diameter of the watered region? Use 3.14 for pi.
o: 6 m

n.0: 6 m is the radius; the diameter is twice the radius.
n.2: This divides the area by 2π (6.28), as if A = 2πr.
n.3: 36 is r²; take its square root to find r, then double it.

Measurement & Geometry.q: A circular pool with a radius of 9 feet is surrounded by a concrete walkway 3 feet wide. A fence will be built along the outer edge of the walkway. How long will the fence be? Use 3.14 for pi.
Measurement & Geometry.w: Outer radius = 9 + 3 = 12 ft. C = 2πr = 2 × 3.14 × 12 = 75.36 ft.

n.0: This is the area inside the fence (3.14 × 12²), not its length.
n.2: This uses the pool's radius (9 ft); the fence is at the outer edge, 12 ft from the center.
n.3: This adds the 3-foot walkway to the diameter once (21 ft); it adds 3 ft on each side (24 ft).

Measurement & Geometry.q: The minute hand of a wall clock in a nurses' station is 15 centimeters long. How far does the tip of the minute hand travel in 20 minutes? Use 3.14 for pi.
Measurement & Geometry.w: In 20 minutes the hand turns 20/60 = 1/3 of a circle. C = 2 × 3.14 × 15 = 94.2 cm. 94.2 ÷ 3 = 31.4 cm.

n.1: This takes 2/3 of the circumference; 20 minutes is 1/3 of an hour.
n.2: This takes 1/3 of πr (3.14 × 15) instead of 1/3 of 2πr.
n.3: This is the distance for a full hour, one complete circle.

Measurement & Geometry.q: A round table has a diameter of 5 feet. Each person seated at the table needs 2 feet of space along the table's edge. What is the greatest number of people who can be seated at the table? Use 3.14 for pi.
Measurement & Geometry.w: C = πd = 3.14 × 5 = 15.7 ft. 15.7 ÷ 2 = 7.85, so 7 people can be seated.

n.0: 15.7 ÷ 2 = 7.85, and an eighth person would not have a full 2 feet, so round down.
n.1: This uses the table's area (19.625 ft²) instead of the distance around it.
n.2: This uses the radius in C = πd (7.85 ft), which halves the edge length.

Measurement & Geometry.q: A rectangular storage bin in a hospital supply room is 2.5 feet long, 2 feet wide, and 1.5 feet tall. How many cubic feet of supplies can the bin hold when it is filled to the top?
o: 6 ft³
7.5 ft³
23.5 ft³
3.75 ft³

n.0: This adds the three dimensions; volume multiplies them.
n.2: 23.5 is the surface area of the bin in square feet, 2(5 + 3.75 + 3), not its volume.
n.3: This multiplies the length by the height (2.5 × 1.5) but leaves out the width.

Measurement & Geometry.q: A cylindrical water tank behind a rural clinic has a radius of 3 feet and a height of 5 feet. What is the volume of the tank? Use 3.14 for pi.
o: 94.2 ft³
47.1 ft³

n.1: This uses the diameter (6 ft) as the radius.
n.2: This uses 2πrh, the area of the curved side, instead of πr²h.
n.3: This multiplies pi by the radius once (3.14 × 3 × 5) instead of by r².

Measurement & Geometry.q: A rectangular fish tank in a pediatric waiting room measures 50 centimeters long, 30 centimeters wide, and 40 centimeters high. How many liters of water does the tank hold when it is completely full?
o: 6 L

n.0: This divides 60,000 cm³ by 100; 1 L = 1,000 cm³.
n.2: This divides 60,000 cm³ by 10,000 instead of 1,000.
n.3: 60,000 is the volume in cubic centimeters (milliliters), not liters.

Measurement & Geometry.q: A cube-shaped gift box has edges 4 inches long. A second cube-shaped box has edges twice as long as the edges of the first box. What is the volume of the second box?
o: 512 in³
256 in³
384 in³
128 in³
Measurement & Geometry.w: Each edge of the second box is 2 × 4 = 8 in. V = 8³ = 8 × 8 × 8 = 512 in³, which is 8 times the first box's 64 in³.

n.1: This multiplies the volume by 4, which is the scale factor for area, not volume.
n.2: 384 is the surface area of the larger cube in square inches (6 × 8²), not its volume.
n.3: This doubles the first box's volume (2 × 64); doubling every edge multiplies volume by 2 × 2 × 2 = 8.

Measurement & Geometry.q: A cylindrical can has a diameter of 8 centimeters and a height of 12 centimeters. How many milliliters can the can hold? Use 3.14 for pi and 1 cubic centimeter = 1 milliliter. Enter the number of milliliters, rounded to the nearest whole number.

tr.301: Multiplied pi by the diameter and the height (3.14 × 8 × 12) without squaring the radius.
tr.2412: Used the diameter (8 cm) as the radius: 3.14 × 64 × 12 = 2,411.52.

Measurement & Geometry.w: r = 8 ÷ 2 = 4 cm. V = πr²h = 3.14 × 16 × 12 = 602.88 cm³ = 602.88 mL, which rounds to 603 mL.

Measurement & Geometry.q: A closed rectangular box measures 10 inches long, 6 inches wide, and 4 inches high. How many square inches of wrapping paper are needed to cover the entire outside of the box with no overlap? Enter the number of square inches.

tr.124: Added the three different faces once; each face has a matching opposite face.
tr.240: Found the volume (10 × 6 × 4) instead of the surface area.

Measurement & Geometry.q: Five containers are being compared for a supply room. Use 3.14 for pi and 1 milliliter = 1 cubic centimeter. Place the containers in order from least volume to greatest volume, starting with the least.
o: A bottle that holds 0.95 L
A cube with 10 cm edges
A jug that holds 1,020 mL
A box 8 cm by 12 cm by 11 cm
A cylinder with radius 5 cm and height 12 cm
Measurement & Geometry.w: Convert each to cubic centimeters: cylinder = 3.14 × 5² × 12 = 942; bottle = 0.95 L = 950 mL = 950; cube = 10³ = 1,000; jug = 1,020; box = 8 × 12 × 11 = 1,056. Least to greatest: 942, 950, 1,000, 1,020, 1,056.

Measurement & Geometry.q: A cone-shaped paper water cup has a radius of 3 centimeters and a height of 10 centimeters. What is the volume of the cup when it is filled to the brim? Use 3.14 for pi.
o: 31.4 cm³
94.2 cm³

n.0: This uses r instead of r²: 1/3 × 3.14 × 3 × 10.
n.1: This uses the cylinder formula πr²h; a cone holds 1/3 of that.
n.3: This uses the diameter (6 cm) as the radius.

Measurement & Geometry.q: A rectangular wading pool is 20 feet long and 10 feet wide and will be filled to a depth of 4 feet. Use 1 cubic foot = 7.5 gallons. A hose fills the pool at 50 gallons per minute. How many hours will it take to fill the pool?
o: 2 hours
0.27 hour
1.2 hours
120 hours

n.1: This divides the 800 cubic feet by the rate (16 minutes) without converting to gallons.
n.2: This reads 120 minutes as 1.2 hours; 120 ÷ 60 = 2 hours.
n.3: 120 is the time in minutes; it must be divided by 60 to give hours.

Measurement & Geometry.q: A rectangular planter box holds 9 cubic feet of soil when filled to the top. The base of the box is 4 feet long and 1.5 feet wide. How deep is the planter box, in inches?
o: 18 in
1.5 in
27 in
15 in

n.1: 1.5 is the depth in feet; 1.5 ft × 12 = 18 in.
n.2: This divides by the length (9 ÷ 4 = 2.25 ft) but leaves out the width.
n.3: This treats 1.5 ft as 15 in, as if a foot had 10 inches; 1.5 ft = 18 in.

Measurement & Geometry.q: A closed cylindrical can has a radius of 3 inches and a height of 8 inches. A paper label covers the curved side of the can but not the top or bottom. What is the area of the label? Use 3.14 for pi.
Measurement & Geometry.w: Unrolled, the label is a rectangle: circumference × height. Area = 2πrh = 2 × 3.14 × 3 × 8 = 150.72 in².

n.0: This uses πrh; the curved side's area is 2πrh (circumference × height).
n.1: 226.08 is the volume (πr²h) in cubic inches, not the label's area.
n.2: This adds the top and bottom circles (2 × 28.26 in²); the label covers the curved side.

Measurement & Geometry.q: A storage room is 4 yards long, 3 yards wide, and 3 yards high. A ventilation fan is sized by the number of cubic feet of air in the room. What is the volume of the room in cubic feet?
o: 36 ft³
108 ft³
324 ft³
972 ft³
Measurement & Geometry.w: V = 4 × 3 × 3 = 36 yd³. 36 × 27 = 972 ft³. (Or convert first: 12 ft × 9 ft × 9 ft = 972 ft³.)

n.0: 36 is the volume in cubic yards, not cubic feet.
n.1: This multiplies 36 yd³ by 3; 1 yd³ = 3 × 3 × 3 = 27 ft³.
n.2: This multiplies 36 yd³ by 9, which is the square-yard factor.

Measurement & Geometry.q: A 13-foot ladder leans against the wall of a building. The foot of the ladder rests on level ground 5 feet from the base of the wall. How high up the wall does the top of the ladder reach?
o: 4 ft
8 ft
12 ft
Measurement & Geometry.w: The ladder is the hypotenuse. h² = 13² - 5² = 169 - 25 = 144, so h = 12 ft (a 5-12-13 right triangle).

n.0: This subtracts 5 instead of 5² (169 - 5 = 164, and the square root of 164 is about 12.8).
n.1: This doubles each length instead of squaring it (26 - 10 = 16, and the square root of 16 is 4).
n.2: This subtracts the lengths (13 - 5); the Pythagorean theorem works with the squares of the sides.

Measurement & Geometry.q: A rectangular television screen is 48 inches wide and 20 inches tall. Screen size is measured along the diagonal from one corner to the opposite corner. What is the diagonal length of the screen?
o: 68 in
52 in

n.0: This subtracts the squares (2,304 - 400); the diagonal is the hypotenuse, so add them.
n.1: This adds the sides (48 + 20); the diagonal is found with a² + b² = c².
n.3: This doubles 20 instead of squaring it (2,304 + 40 = 2,344, and the square root of 2,344 is about 48.4).

Measurement & Geometry.q: In triangle PQR, angle P measures 38°, and angle Q measures twice as much as angle P. A student needs the third angle to finish a drawing. What is the measure of angle R?

n.1: This finds the complement of angle P (90 - 38); the angles of a triangle sum to 180°.
n.2: This subtracts angle P (180 - 38) but not angle Q.
n.3: This subtracts angle Q (180 - 76) but not angle P; both must be subtracted.

Measurement & Geometry.q: Two straight roads cross each other, forming four angles at the intersection. One of the angles measures 57°. What are the measures of the angle vertical (directly opposite) to it and of an angle adjacent to it?
o: Vertical: 123°; adjacent: 57°
Vertical: 57°; adjacent: 33°
Vertical: 57°; adjacent: 123°
Vertical: 33°; adjacent: 147°
Measurement & Geometry.w: Vertical angles are equal, so the opposite angle is 57°. An adjacent angle forms a straight line with the 57° angle, so it is 180 - 57 = 123°.

n.0: This reverses the rules. Vertical angles are equal (57°); adjacent angles on a straight line are supplementary (123°).
n.1: This uses 90° for the adjacent angle; angles along a straight line sum to 180°.
n.3: This takes the complement for the vertical angle; vertical angles are equal.

Measurement & Geometry.q: A rectangular park is 240 meters long and 100 meters wide. Instead of walking along two sides of the park to reach the opposite corner, a jogger takes a straight diagonal path. How many meters shorter is the diagonal route? Enter the number of meters.

tr.200: Used 240 - 100 = 140 m as the diagonal instead of the Pythagorean theorem.
tr.260: Gave the length of the diagonal instead of the distance saved.
tr.340: Gave the distance along the two sides instead of the distance saved.

Measurement & Geometry.q: The roof truss of a house is an isosceles triangle. The angle at the peak, between the two equal sloping sides, measures 112°. What is the measure of each of the two base angles of the truss?
Measurement & Geometry.w: In an isosceles triangle the two base angles are equal. (180 - 112) ÷ 2 = 68 ÷ 2 = 34°.

n.0: This uses 360°, the angle sum of a quadrilateral, instead of 180°.
n.1: 68° is both base angles together (180 - 112); divide by 2.
n.3: This halves the peak angle; the base angles share what is left of 180°.

Measurement & Geometry.q: A gazebo floor is shaped like a regular hexagon. A carpenter needs the angle at each corner to cut the floorboards. What is the measure of each interior angle of the floor?
Measurement & Geometry.w: Sum of interior angles = (n - 2) × 180 = (6 - 2) × 180 = 720°. Each angle = 720 ÷ 6 = 120°.

n.1: 108° is each interior angle of a regular pentagon (5 sides).
n.2: 720° is the sum of all six interior angles; divide by 6.
n.3: 60° is each exterior angle (360 ÷ 6); an interior angle and its exterior angle sum to 180°.

Measurement & Geometry.q: At the same time of day, a 6-foot-tall nurse casts a shadow 4 feet long, and a flagpole outside the clinic casts a shadow 22 feet long. The two right triangles formed are similar. How tall is the flagpole?
o: 33 ft
24 ft
132 ft
Measurement & Geometry.w: Height to shadow is the same in both triangles: 6/4 = h/22. h = 22 × 6 ÷ 4 = 33 ft.

n.1: This sets up the ratio upside down (22 × 4 ÷ 6).
n.2: This adds the 2-foot difference between height and shadow; similar triangles scale by multiplying.
n.3: This multiplies 6 by 22 but does not divide by the 4-foot shadow.

Measurement & Geometry.q: Two angles in a shelf bracket design are complementary. The larger angle measures 12° more than twice the smaller angle. What is the measure of the larger angle?
Measurement & Geometry.w: Let the smaller angle be x. x + (2x + 12) = 90, so 3x = 78 and x = 26. Larger = 2(26) + 12 = 64°. Check: 26 + 64 = 90.

n.0: This uses 180° (supplementary): 3x + 12 = 180 gives x = 56 and a larger angle of 124°.
n.1: This leaves out the 12°: 3x = 90 gives x = 30 and a larger angle of 60°.
n.3: 26° is the smaller angle; the larger is 2(26) + 12 = 64°.

Measurement & Geometry.q: A student is sorting triangles by type for a geometry project. Which set of side lengths forms a right triangle?
o: 8 cm, 15 cm, and 18 cm
6 cm, 9 cm, and 12 cm
7 cm, 24 cm, and 25 cm
5 cm, 12 cm, and 14 cm
Measurement & Geometry.w: Test a² + b² = c² with the longest side as c: 7² + 24² = 49 + 576 = 625 = 25². Only this set satisfies the Pythagorean theorem.

n.0: 8² + 15² = 289, which is 17², not 18² = 324.
n.3: 5² + 12² = 169, which is 13², not 14² = 196.

Measurement & Geometry.q: A triangle has two angles that measure 35° and 55°. Which statements about the triangle must be true? Select all that apply.
o: The 35° and 55° angles are complementary.
The 35° and 55° angles are supplementary.
The third angle measures 90°.
It is an acute triangle.
It is an isosceles triangle.
The longest side is opposite the third angle.
Measurement & Geometry.w: Third angle = 180 - 35 - 55 = 90°, so it is a right triangle. 35 + 55 = 90, so those two angles are complementary. The longest side (the hypotenuse) is opposite the largest angle, the 90° angle.

n.1: 35° + 55° = 90°, so the angles are complementary; supplementary angles sum to 180°.
n.3: The third angle is 90°, so it is a right triangle; an acute triangle has all three angles under 90°.
n.4: The angles 35°, 55° and 90° are all different, so no two sides are equal; the triangle is scalene.

Measurement & Geometry.q: A right triangle has a hypotenuse of 17 centimeters and one leg of 8 centimeters. A designer needs the triangle's area to plan a tile pattern. What is the area of the triangle?
o: 136 cm²
60 cm²
120 cm²
68 cm²
Measurement & Geometry.w: Other leg: 17² - 8² = 289 - 64 = 225, so the leg is 15 cm. A = 1/2 × 8 × 15 = 60 cm².

n.0: This multiplies the given leg by the hypotenuse (8 × 17) with no 1/2.
n.2: This multiplies the legs (8 × 15) but leaves out the 1/2.
n.3: This uses the hypotenuse as the height (1/2 × 8 × 17); the two legs are the base and height.

Data, Statistics & Variables.q: In a pictograph of blood donations, each full blood-drop icon represents 12 units and each half icon represents 6 units. The rows show Monday 4 1/2 icons, Tuesday 3 icons, Wednesday 6 icons, and Thursday 2 1/2 icons. How many units of blood were donated over the four days?

n.0: 16 is the number of icons, not the number of units they represent.
n.1: 204 = 17 x 12 counts each half icon as a full icon.
n.3: 180 = 15 x 12 drops both half icons.

Data, Statistics & Variables.q: A line graph shows an infant's weight at monthly checkups, with the vertical axis marked every 2 pounds. Birth: on the 8-pound line. 1 month: halfway between 10 and 12. 2 months: on the 12-pound line. 3 months: halfway between 12 and 14. 4 months: on the 14-pound line. What was the mean weight gain per month from birth to 4 months?
o: 6 pounds
1.5 pounds
3 pounds
1.2 pounds
Data, Statistics & Variables.w: Total gain = 14 - 8 = 6 pounds over 4 months (birth to month 4 is 4 intervals). Mean gain = 6 / 4 = 1.5 pounds per month.

n.0: 6 pounds is the total gain over 4 months, not the gain per month.
n.2: 3 pounds is the gain in the first month only (8 to 11, the point halfway between 10 and 12).
n.3: 6 / 5 = 1.2 divides by the 5 checkups instead of the 4 one-month intervals between them.

Data, Statistics & Variables.q: A stacked bar graph shows clinic visits by age group. The April bar reaches 240 visits in total. Its 'Under 18' segment runs from 0 to 70, its '18 to 64' segment from 70 to 185, and its '65 and older' segment from 185 to 240. To the nearest tenth of a percent, what percent of April visits were by patients aged 18 to 64?
Data, Statistics & Variables.w: A middle segment's value is its top minus its bottom: 185 - 70 = 115 visits. 115 / 240 = 0.4792, or 47.9%.

n.1: 185 / 240 = 77.1% reads the top edge of the segment (185) as its value instead of subtracting the 70 below it.
n.2: 55 / 240 = 22.9% is the '65 and older' segment (240 - 185).
n.3: 70 / 240 = 29.2% is the 'Under 18' segment.

Data, Statistics & Variables.q: A patient's oral intake record for one day shows: 8 a.m. water 240 mL, 10 a.m. juice 180 mL, noon soup 360 mL, 3 p.m. tea 120 mL, 6 p.m. milk 300 mL. What percent of the day's total intake was taken before noon? Enter the number only, without the percent sign.

tr.420: the milliliters before noon, not the percent

Data, Statistics & Variables.q: A pharmacy table lists units on hand and average daily use: Drug A 180 on hand, 12 per day; Drug B 95, 8 per day; Drug C 240, 30 per day; Drug D 130, 9 per day; Drug E 210, 14 per day; Drug F 66, 5 per day. A drug is reordered when it has fewer than 14 days of supply left. Which drugs should be reordered? Select all that apply.
o: Drug C
Drug B
Drug E
Drug D
Drug A
Drug F
Data, Statistics & Variables.w: Days of supply = units on hand / daily use. A: 180 / 12 = 15. B: 95 / 8 = 11.9. C: 240 / 30 = 8. D: 130 / 9 = 14.4. E: 210 / 14 = 15. F: 66 / 5 = 13.2. Fewer than 14 days: B, C and F. Drug C has the most units on hand but the shortest supply.

n.2: 210 / 14 = 15 days; the daily use of 14 is not the number of days left.
n.3: 130 / 9 = 14.4 days, just above the 14-day threshold.
n.4: 180 / 12 = 15 days, which is not fewer than 14.

Data, Statistics & Variables.q: A double bar graph shows hospital admissions by unit in 2024 and 2025: Cardiac 320 and 368; Orthopedics 250 and 275; Pediatrics 180 and 216; Oncology 400 and 436. Which unit had the greatest percent increase in admissions from 2024 to 2025?
o: Cardiac
Oncology
Orthopedics
Pediatrics
Data, Statistics & Variables.w: Percent increase = change / 2024 value. Cardiac 48 / 320 = 15%. Orthopedics 25 / 250 = 10%. Pediatrics 36 / 180 = 20%. Oncology 36 / 400 = 9%. Pediatrics is greatest.

n.0: Cardiac had the largest increase in number (48), but 48 / 320 is only 15%.
n.1: Oncology has the tallest bars, but its 36 extra admissions are only 9% of 400.
n.2: Orthopedics rose 25 / 250 = 10%.

Data, Statistics & Variables.q: A line graph shows the number of registered nurses employed in a county: 2000, 12,000; 2005, 13,500; 2015, 15,500; 2020, 16,800. The years on the horizontal axis are plotted to scale. During which interval was the average increase per year the greatest?
Data, Statistics & Variables.w: Divide each change by the number of years. 2000 to 2005: 1,500 / 5 = 300 per year. 2005 to 2015: 2,000 / 10 = 200 per year. 2015 to 2020: 1,300 / 5 = 260 per year. 2005 to 2020: 3,300 / 15 = 220 per year. The greatest is 2000 to 2005.

n.1: This interval has the largest total increase (2,000), but it covers 10 years, so it averages 200 per year.
n.2: 1,300 over 5 years is 260 per year, less than the 300 per year from 2000 to 2005.
n.3: 3,300 over 15 years averages 220 per year.

Data, Statistics & Variables.q: A table summarizes a screening test given to 500 people. Tested positive and have the condition: 45. Tested positive and do not have the condition: 15. Tested negative and have the condition: 5. Tested negative and do not have the condition: 435. Of the people who tested positive, what percent actually have the condition? Enter the number only.

tr.12: the percent of all 500 people who tested positive
tr.90: 45 out of the 50 people who have the condition

Data, Statistics & Variables.w: 'Of the people who tested positive' sets the denominator: 45 + 15 = 60. Of these, 45 have the condition. 45 / 60 = 0.75 = 75%.

Data, Statistics & Variables.q: Maya's monthly budget of $2,400 is shown in a pie chart: Rent 35%, Food 15%, Transportation 12.5%, Savings 10%, Other 27.5%. How much more does she budget for rent than for food and transportation combined?
Data, Statistics & Variables.w: Amount = percent x total. Rent: 0.35 x 2,400 = $840. Food: 0.15 x 2,400 = $360. Transportation: 0.125 x 2,400 = $300. Food + transportation = $660. Difference: 840 - 660 = $180.

n.1: 840 - 300 = $540 compares rent with transportation only.
n.2: 840 - 360 = $480 compares rent with food only.
n.3: $660 is the food and transportation total, not how much more rent is.

Data, Statistics & Variables.q: A pie chart shows the blood types of 400 patients. Of these patients, 152 have type O blood. What is the central angle of the type O sector?
Data, Statistics & Variables.w: Fraction of the whole: 152 / 400 = 0.38. Central angle = 0.38 x 360° = 136.8°.

n.1: 38 is the percent (38%), not the angle; it must be multiplied by 360° as a decimal.
n.2: 152 is the number of patients, not degrees.
n.3: 0.62 x 360° = 223.2° is the angle for all the patients who are not type O.

Data, Statistics & Variables.q:
A stem-and-leaf plot shows the ages of patients seen at a clinic one morning (key: 3 | 1 = 31 years).
2 | 3 7 9
3 | 1 1 4 8
4 | 0 2 5 5 5 6
5 | 2 7
How many patients were older than 30 but younger than 45?
Data, Statistics & Variables.w: Ages greater than 30 and less than 45: 31, 31, 34, 38, 40, 42. That is 6 patients. The three 45s are not younger than 45.

n.0: 4 counts only the 3 stem (31, 31, 34, 38) and misses 40 and 42.
n.1: 9 includes the three patients aged 45, who are not younger than 45.
n.3: 10 counts every leaf on the 3 and 4 stems, including 45, 45, 45 and 46.

Data, Statistics & Variables.q: A histogram shows weekly study hours for a class of nursing students: 0-4 hours, 3 students; 5-9 hours, 8 students; 10-14 hours, 12 students; 15-19 hours, 5 students; 20-24 hours, 2 students. What percent of the students studied at least 10 hours? Round to the nearest tenth and enter the number only.

tr.19: the number of students, not the percent
tr.36.7: the percent who studied fewer than 10 hours

Data, Statistics & Variables.q: A histogram shows the systolic blood pressures of 50 adults: 100-109, 6 adults; 110-119, 14 adults; 120-129, 17 adults; 130-139, 9 adults; 140-149, 4 adults. Which statement must be true?
o: Over half the adults had pressures of 130 or above
Exactly 4 adults had a systolic pressure of 140
The median pressure is in the 120-129 interval
The most common single reading was 125
Data, Statistics & Variables.w: With 50 values, the median is the mean of the 25th and 26th values. Running totals: 6, then 20, then 37. The 25th and 26th values both fall in the 120-129 interval.

n.0: Only 9 + 4 = 13 of 50 adults (26%) were at 130 or above.
n.1: The 4 adults are somewhere in 140-149; a histogram does not show exact values.
n.3: The tallest bar shows the most common interval, not any single reading.

Data, Statistics & Variables.q: A dot plot shows the number of missed medication doses reported by 20 patients: 0 doses, 7 dots; 1 dose, 5 dots; 2 doses, 4 dots; 3 doses, 2 dots; 4 doses, 1 dot; 6 doses, 1 dot. What fraction of the patients missed 2 or more doses?
Data, Statistics & Variables.w: Patients with 2 or more missed doses: 4 + 2 + 1 + 1 = 8. 8 / 20 = 2/5.

n.0: 4 / 20 = 1/5 counts only 3 or more doses, leaving out the 4 patients who missed exactly 2.
n.2: 12 / 20 = 3/5 is the fraction who missed fewer than 2 doses.
n.3: 13 / 20 counts everyone who missed 1 or more doses.

Data, Statistics & Variables.q: A box plot of waiting times, in minutes, at a walk-in clinic shows a minimum of 4, a first quartile of 11, a median of 18, a third quartile of 27, and a maximum of 52. Which statement is supported by the plot?
o: About 25% of the patients waited over 18 minutes
About half the waits were 11 to 27 minutes
The interquartile range was 48 minutes
The mean waiting time was 18 minutes
Data, Statistics & Variables.w: The box runs from Q1 (11) to Q3 (27) and holds the middle 50% of the data, so about half the waits were between 11 and 27 minutes.

n.0: About 50% of the values lie above the median of 18, not 25%.
n.2: 52 - 4 = 48 is the range. The IQR is 27 - 11 = 16 minutes.
n.3: 18 is the median; a box plot does not show the mean.

Data, Statistics & Variables.q: In a pie chart of a clinic's annual expenses, the medical supplies sector has a central angle of 54°. Medical supplies cost $13,500 for the year. What were the clinic's total annual expenses? Enter the number of dollars only, without commas.

tr.15: the supplies percent, not the total
tr.250: 13,500 / 54, treating the angle as the percent
tr.2025: 13,500 x 0.15, applying the percent instead of dividing by it

Data, Statistics & Variables.w: Fraction of the whole: 54 / 360 = 0.15 (15%). Supplies = 0.15 x total, so total = 13,500 / 0.15 = $90,000.

Data, Statistics & Variables.q:
A stem-and-leaf plot shows hemoglobin levels, in g/dL, for 11 blood donors (key: 12 | 4 = 12.4).
11 | 2 6 8
12 | 0 4 4 9
13 | 1 5 7
14 | 3
How many donors had a hemoglobin level below 12.5 g/dL?
Data, Statistics & Variables.w: Values below 12.5: 11.2, 11.6, 11.8, 12.0, 12.4, 12.4. Each leaf is one donor, so the repeated 4 counts twice: 6 donors.

n.0: 7 includes 12.9, which is above 12.5.
n.1: 5 counts the repeated leaf 12.4 once; each leaf is a separate donor.
n.3: 3 counts only the 11 stem and misses 12.0, 12.4 and 12.4.

Data, Statistics & Variables.q: A school nurse surveys 270 students about how they get to school and plans a pie chart of the results: walk 45, bus 81, car 126, bike 18. What central angle should the bus sector have?
Data, Statistics & Variables.w: Bus fraction: 81 / 270 = 0.3. Central angle = 0.3 x 360° = 108°.

n.0: 126 / 270 x 360° = 168° is the car sector.
n.1: 81 is the number of bus riders, not degrees.
n.3: 30 is the percent (30%); as a decimal it must be multiplied by 360°.

Data, Statistics & Variables.q: A histogram shows the birth weights of 40 infants: 5.0-5.9 lb, 3 infants; 6.0-6.9 lb, 9 infants; 7.0-7.9 lb, 15 infants; 8.0-8.9 lb, 10 infants; 9.0-9.9 lb, 3 infants. Which statement is supported by the histogram?
o: More than one-third of the infants weighed 8.0 pounds or more
Fewer than 1 in 3 infants weighed under 7.0 pounds
Exactly 15 infants weighed 7.5 pounds
The heaviest infant weighed 9.9 pounds
Data, Statistics & Variables.w: Under 7.0 lb: 3 + 9 = 12 infants. 12 / 40 = 30%, which is less than 1/3 (about 33.3%).

n.0: 10 + 3 = 13 infants, and 13 / 40 = 32.5%, which is less than one-third (33.3%).
n.2: The 15 infants weighed somewhere from 7.0 to 7.9 lb; a histogram does not give single values.
n.3: The top interval shows only that the heaviest infants weighed between 9.0 and 9.9 lb.

Data, Statistics & Variables.q: A pie chart shows the preferred shifts of 600 hospital staff members: Day 38%, Evening 22%, and the rest split between Night and Rotating. The Night sector is three times as large as the Rotating sector. How many staff members prefer the night shift?
Data, Statistics & Variables.w: Remaining percent: 100 - 38 - 22 = 40%. Night is 3 parts and Rotating 1 part, so Night = 3/4 x 40% = 30%. 0.30 x 600 = 180.

n.1: 60 is the Rotating group (10% of 600).
n.2: 240 is the whole remaining 40%, Night and Rotating together.
n.3: 120 splits the remaining 40% evenly (20% each) instead of 3 to 1.

Data, Statistics & Variables.q: A scatterplot shows the hours of sleep the night before (x) and reaction time on a driving test, in milliseconds (y), for 25 adults. The points fall close to a straight line that slopes downward from left to right. Which best describes the relationship?
o: No correlation
Strong positive correlation
Weak negative correlation
Strong negative correlation
Data, Statistics & Variables.w: A downward slope from left to right means that as x increases, y tends to decrease: a negative correlation. Points close to a line make it strong.

n.0: No correlation is a cloud with no direction; these points follow a clear line.
n.1: A positive correlation rises from left to right; this pattern falls.
n.2: A weak correlation has widely scattered points; these fall close to the line.

Data, Statistics & Variables.q: A health class lists four pairs of variables that could be graphed on scatterplots. Which pair would most likely show a negative correlation?
o: Outdoor temperature and monthly heating cost
Household size and weekly grocery spending
A child's height and arm span
Hours worked and gross weekly pay
Data, Statistics & Variables.w: As outdoor temperature rises, less heating is needed, so heating cost tends to fall: one variable increases while the other decreases.

n.1: Larger households tend to spend more on groceries, a positive correlation.
n.2: Taller children tend to have longer arm spans, a positive correlation.
n.3: More hours worked brings more gross pay, a positive correlation.

Data, Statistics & Variables.q: The table lists hours of exercise per week (x) and resting heart rate in beats per minute (y) for seven adults: (1, 82), (2, 79), (3, 76), (4, 74), (5, 70), (6, 69), (7, 65). Which statement best describes the relationship shown in a scatterplot of these data?
o: Heart rate tends to fall as weekly exercise hours rise
Exercise hours tend to rise as heart rate rises
There is no correlation, since the drops are uneven
Heart rate falls by exactly 3 beats per extra hour
Data, Statistics & Variables.w: As x goes from 1 to 7, y goes from 82 to 65, so y tends to decrease as x increases: a negative correlation.

n.1: Heart rate falls as exercise rises; the two move in opposite directions, not together.
n.2: Uneven drops (3, 3, 2, 4, 1, 4) still form a steady downward trend; no correlation would show no direction at all.
n.3: The drops are 3, 3, 2, 4, 1 and 4 beats, so the decrease is not exactly 3 each hour.

Data, Statistics & Variables.q: The table lists hours studied (x) and exam score (y) for seven students: (2, 61), (3, 66), (4, 70), (5, 52), (6, 79), (7, 83), (8, 88). When the data are graphed on a scatterplot, which point does not fit the overall trend?
Data, Statistics & Variables.w: Scores rise about 4 to 5 points per extra hour, so a student who studied 5 hours would be expected to score about 74. A score of 52 sits far below the pattern.

n.0: (8, 88) is the highest point, but it continues the upward trend.
n.1: (4, 70) is about 4 points above (3, 66), in line with the trend.
n.3: (2, 61) has the lowest x-value, and its score fits the rising pattern from the left.

Data, Statistics & Variables.q: A study of 30 hospitals found a strong positive correlation between the number of parking spaces and the number of patient falls reported each year. Which conclusion is best supported by this finding?
o: Reducing parking spaces will reduce patient falls
The link is a coincidence, since parking cannot affect falls
Adding parking spaces will lead to more patient falls
Both may rise with a third factor, such as hospital size
Data, Statistics & Variables.w: Correlation does not show causation. Larger hospitals have more parking and more patients, so more falls are reported; a third variable can explain both.

n.0: This also assumes cause and effect, just in the other direction of change.
n.1: A strong correlation across 30 hospitals is a real pattern, not chance; a third variable such as hospital size explains it.
n.2: This claims parking causes falls; a correlation alone does not show cause and effect.

Data, Statistics & Variables.q: A trend line on a scatterplot of weekly study hours (x) and exam score (y) passes through the points (4, 68) and (10, 83). Using the trend line, what exam score is predicted for a student who studies 12 hours per week?
Data, Statistics & Variables.w: Slope = (83 - 68) / (10 - 4) = 15 / 6 = 2.5 points per hour. From (10, 83), 2 more hours adds 2 x 2.5 = 5, so the prediction is 88.

n.0: 83 + 2.5 adds the slope once, but 12 hours is 2 hours beyond 10.
n.2: Using 6 / 15 = 0.4 inverts the slope (run over rise), giving 83 + 0.8.
n.3: 83 / 10 x 12 = 99.6 treats the line as passing through the origin (direct variation), but it starts at 58.

Data, Statistics & Variables.q: A scatterplot of children's ages, in years (x), and heights, in inches (y), has a trend line passing through (3, 37) and (8, 50). According to the trend line, how many inches does height increase for each additional year of age? Enter your answer as a decimal.

tr.13: the total change in height, not the change per year
tr.6.25: 50 / 8, a single point's ratio instead of the change

Data, Statistics & Variables.w: Slope = change in y / change in x = (50 - 37) / (8 - 3) = 13 / 5 = 2.6 inches per year.

Data, Statistics & Variables.q: A trend line was fit to data on daily water intake and age for a sample of adults aged 20 to 60. For which age is a prediction made from the trend line least reliable?
o: 41 years
85 years
25 years
58 years
Data, Statistics & Variables.w: Predicting within the range of the data (interpolation) is reasonable. Age 85 is far outside the 20 to 60 range, so that prediction is an extrapolation and the least reliable.

n.0: 41 is near the middle of the data, where the trend line is best supported.
n.2: 25 is inside the 20 to 60 range, so it is an interpolation.
n.3: 58 is near the upper end but still inside the 20 to 60 range of the data.

Data, Statistics & Variables.q: The trend line for a scatterplot of hours since a dose (x) and drug concentration in the blood, in mcg/mL (y), is y = -1.8x + 24. According to the trend line, after how many hours will the concentration be 9 mcg/mL? Round to the nearest tenth.

tr.7.8: substituting 9 for x (24 - 16.2) instead of for y

Data, Statistics & Variables.q: A student is choosing data sets to graph on scatterplots for a class project. Which pairs of variables would most likely show a positive correlation? Select all that apply.
o: Hours of TV watched per day and test scores
Cigarettes smoked per day and lung capacity
Number of absences and final course grade
Weight of a package and its shipping cost
A person's height and arm span
Minutes spent jogging and calories burned
Data, Statistics & Variables.w: Positive correlation: both variables tend to increase together. Taller people have longer arm spans, longer jogs burn more calories, and heavier packages cost more to ship.

n.0: More TV time tends to go with lower test scores, a negative correlation.
n.1: More smoking tends to go with lower lung capacity, a negative correlation.
n.2: More absences tend to go with lower grades, a negative correlation.

Data, Statistics & Variables.q: A trend line relating certified nursing assistants' years of experience (x) to hourly wage in dollars (y) is y = 0.75x + 16.50. What does the 0.75 represent?
o: The predicted wage increase for each additional year
The predicted number of years needed to earn $16.50
The predicted hourly wage after one year of experience
The predicted starting wage for a CNA with no experience
Data, Statistics & Variables.w: In y = mx + b, the slope m is the change in y for each 1-unit increase in x. Here wages are predicted to rise $0.75 per hour for each additional year.

n.1: $16.50 is predicted at 0 years; 0.75 is a rate, not a number of years.
n.2: After one year the predicted wage is 0.75 + 16.50 = $17.25, not $0.75.
n.3: The starting wage (x = 0) is the y-intercept, $16.50.

Data, Statistics & Variables.q: A clinic's trend line for monthly advertising spending, x (in hundreds of dollars), and new patients, y, is y = 4x + 30. In March the clinic spent $1,200 on advertising and gained 70 new patients. How does March compare with the trend line's prediction?
o: 35.2 more than predicted
8 more than predicted
8 fewer than predicted
22 more than predicted
Data, Statistics & Variables.w: $1,200 is 12 hundred dollars, so x = 12. Predicted y = 4(12) + 30 = 78. Actual 70 is 78 - 70 = 8 fewer than predicted.

n.0: Using x = 1.2 (thousands) gives 4.8 + 30 = 34.8; x is in hundreds, so x = 12.
n.1: The size is right, but 70 is below 78, so March was under the prediction.
n.3: 70 - 48 = 22 uses 4 x 12 and leaves out the 30 in the equation.

Data, Statistics & Variables.q: A nurse records the pulse rates of eight patients, in beats per minute: 72, 88, 64, 90, 76, 70, 84, 68. What is the median pulse rate?
Data, Statistics & Variables.w: Order the values: 64, 68, 70, 72, 76, 84, 88, 90. With 8 values, the median is the mean of the 4th and 5th: (72 + 76) / 2 = 74.

n.0: 612 / 8 = 76.5 is the mean, not the median.
n.1: 76 is only one of the two middle values; with an even count, average the two.
n.3: (90 + 76) / 2 = 83 takes the middle of the list as written, without ordering it first.

Data, Statistics & Variables.q: A uniform store records the sizes of the last 10 pairs of nursing clogs it sold: 8, 9, 7.5, 9, 10, 8, 9, 11, 8.5, 9. What is the mode of the sizes sold?
Data, Statistics & Variables.w: The mode is the value that occurs most often. Size 9 appears 4 times, more than any other size.

n.0: 89 / 10 = 8.9 is the mean of the sizes.
n.1: Size 8 appears only twice, fewer times than size 9.
n.3: 4 is how many times size 9 appears, not the size itself.

Data, Statistics & Variables.q: The daily patient census on a medical unit for one week was 28, 31, 24, 35, 29, 22, and 33. What is the range of the daily census for the week?
Data, Statistics & Variables.w: Range = maximum - minimum = 35 - 22 = 13.

n.0: 33 - 28 = 5 subtracts the first value from the last as listed, not the minimum from the maximum.
n.2: 35 - 24 = 11 uses 24 as the minimum, but 22 is smaller.
n.3: 31 - 22 = 9 uses 31 as the maximum, but 35 is larger.

Data, Statistics & Variables.q: To qualify for an honors program, Jordan needs a mean score of at least 85 on five exams. Jordan's first four scores are 78, 91, 84, and 88. What is the lowest score Jordan can earn on the fifth exam and still qualify?

tr.85: the target mean, not the needed score
tr.85.25: the mean of the first four scores

Data, Statistics & Variables.w: Total needed = mean x count = 85 x 5 = 425. Current total = 78 + 91 + 84 + 88 = 341. Fifth score = 425 - 341 = 84.

Data, Statistics & Variables.q: In a nursing course, exams count for 50% of the final grade, quizzes for 30%, and homework for 20%. Priya's averages are 82 on exams, 90 on quizzes, and 95 on homework. What is Priya's final course grade? Enter the number only.
A morning section of 12 students had a mean quiz score of 75, and an afternoon section of 28 students had a mean quiz score of 85. What is the mean quiz score of all 40 students?

n.0: (12 x 85 + 28 x 75) / 40 = 78 swaps the section sizes.
n.1: The larger section pulls the mean toward 85, but the 12 lower scores still count.
n.3: (75 + 85) / 2 = 80 averages the two means, ignoring that the sections have different sizes.

Data, Statistics & Variables.q: The mean of six lab values is 40. A seventh lab value of 61 is added to the data set. What is the mean of all seven values?
Data, Statistics & Variables.w: Original total = 6 x 40 = 240. New total = 240 + 61 = 301. New mean = 301 / 7 = 43.

n.0: 301 / 6 = 50.2 divides the new total by the old count.
n.2: 40 + 21 / 6 = 43.5 spreads the extra 21 over 6 values instead of 7.
n.3: (40 + 61) / 2 = 50.5 averages the old mean with the new value as if they had equal weight.

Data, Statistics & Variables.q: A survey of 25 households records the number of children in each: 0 children, 4 households; 1 child, 7 households; 2 children, 8 households; 3 children, 4 households; 4 children, 2 households. What is the mean number of children per household? Enter your answer as a decimal.

tr.2: the median or mode, not the mean
tr.5: the mean of the household counts (25 / 5)
tr.8.6: 43 / 5, dividing by the number of categories instead of households

Data, Statistics & Variables.q: A frequency table shows quiz scores for 20 students: a score of 6, 2 students; 7, 4 students; 8, 4 students; 9, 6 students; 10, 4 students. What is the median quiz score?
Data, Statistics & Variables.w: With 20 values, the median is the mean of the 10th and 11th. Running totals: 2, 6, 10, 16, 20. The 10th value is 8 and the 11th is 9, so the median is (8 + 9) / 2 = 8.5.

n.0: 166 / 20 = 8.3 is the mean, not the median.
n.1: 9 is the mode (6 students) and only the 11th value.
n.2: 8 is the middle of the score values 6 to 10 ignoring the frequencies, and it is only the 10th value.

Data, Statistics & Variables.q: A data set of wait times, in minutes, is 12, 15, 15, 18, 20, 22, 38. Which statement about the data set is true?
o: The median of the wait times is 20
The mean exceeds the median
The range of the wait times is 23
The mode of the wait times is 2
Data, Statistics & Variables.w: Mean = 140 / 7 = 20. Median = 4th value = 18. 20 > 18, so the mean is greater than the median (the 38 pulls the mean up).

n.0: 20 is the mean; the median is the middle (4th) value, 18.
n.2: 38 - 15 = 23 uses the mode as the minimum; the range is 38 - 12 = 26.
n.3: 15 appears twice; the mode is 15, not the number of times it appears.

Data, Statistics & Variables.q: The mean of 8 blood glucose readings is 115 mg/dL. When one reading is removed, the mean of the remaining 7 readings is 110 mg/dL. What was the value of the removed reading, in mg/dL?

tr.120: 115 + 5, adding the change in the mean
tr.112.5: the average of the two means

Data, Statistics & Variables.w: Total of 8 readings = 8 x 115 = 920. Total of 7 readings = 7 x 110 = 770. Removed reading = 920 - 770 = 150 mg/dL.

Data, Statistics & Variables.q: The ordered data set 3, 5, 8, 11, 14, 20 has a median of 9.5. A seventh value, 9, is added to the data set. What is the new median?
Data, Statistics & Variables.w: New ordered set: 3, 5, 8, 9, 11, 14, 20. With 7 values, the median is the 4th value, 9.

n.1: 9.5 was the median before the new value was added.
n.2: 70 / 7 = 10 is the new mean.
n.3: (8 + 9) / 2 = 8.5 averages two values, but an odd count has a single middle value.

Data, Statistics & Variables.q: The wait times, in minutes, for seven patients at an urgent care center were 12, 14, 14, 16, 17, 18, and 65. Which measure best describes a typical wait time for these patients, and why?
o: The mean, because it uses every value in the data set
The median, because the 65-minute wait pulls the mean up
The range, because it shows the spread from 12 to 65
The mode, because 14 is the most common wait time
Data, Statistics & Variables.w: The mean is 156 / 7 = 22.3 minutes, higher than six of the seven waits because the outlier 65 pulls it up. The median, 16, is resistant to the outlier and describes a typical wait.

n.0: Using every value is exactly why the mean is distorted here: the 65 drags it above six of the seven waits.
n.2: The range measures spread, not a typical value, and it is inflated by the outlier.
n.3: 14 appears only twice in seven values, so it says little about the center.

Data, Statistics & Variables.q: A histogram of household incomes in a town has a tall peak on the left and a long tail stretching to the right. Which statement about the incomes is most likely true?
o: The mean and median are about equal
The distribution is skewed to the left
The mean is greater than the median
The median is greater than the mean
Data, Statistics & Variables.w: A long tail to the right is a right (positive) skew. The few very high incomes pull the mean toward the tail, so the mean is greater than the median.

n.0: Mean and median are about equal in a symmetric distribution, not a skewed one.
n.1: Skew is named for the tail, not the peak; the tail here is on the right.
n.3: That relationship fits a left-skewed distribution, where the tail is on the low side.

Data, Statistics & Variables.q: On an easy 20-point quiz, most students scored from 18 to 20 points, and a few students scored between 5 and 10 points. Which describes the shape of the score distribution and how its mean compares with its median?
o: Skewed right; the mean is greater than the median
Skewed left; the mean is greater than the median
Skewed left; the mean is less than the median
Skewed right; the mean is less than the median
Data, Statistics & Variables.w: The few low scores form a long tail on the left, so the distribution is skewed left. Those low scores pull the mean down below the median.

n.0: This names the skew by where the scores pile up (the right); skew is named for the tail, which is on the left.
n.1: The shape is right, but the low tail pulls the mean below the median, not above it.
n.3: The tail is on the left, so the distribution is skewed left, not right.

Data, Statistics & Variables.q: Two clinics both have a mean wait time of 20 minutes. The standard deviation of the wait times is 3 minutes at Clinic A and 9 minutes at Clinic B. Which statement is correct?
o: Clinic B's wait times are more spread out around 20 minutes
Clinic B's patients wait longer on average than Clinic A's
Clinic A sees more patients, so its wait times vary less
Clinic A's median wait time is greater than Clinic B's
Data, Statistics & Variables.w: Standard deviation measures spread: roughly the typical distance of values from the mean. A larger SD (9 vs 3) means Clinic B's waits vary more around the shared mean of 20.

n.1: Both clinics have the same mean of 20 minutes; SD describes spread, not the average.
n.2: SD does not depend on the number of patients; nothing in the data gives patient counts.
n.3: Standard deviation gives no information about which median is larger.

Data, Statistics & Variables.q: A data set of daily exercise minutes for seven patients is 4, 6, 7, 7, 9, 10, 41. If the value 41 is removed from the data set, how do the mean and the median change?
o: The mean falls by about 4.8; the median falls to 6.5
The mean and median both fall by about 4.8
The mean falls by about 4.8; the median stays at 7
The mean falls by about 5.9; the median stays at 7
Data, Statistics & Variables.w: Before: mean = 84 / 7 = 12, median = 7. After: 4, 6, 7, 7, 9, 10 has mean 43 / 6 = 7.17 and median (7 + 7) / 2 = 7. The mean drops by about 4.8; the median does not change.

n.0: 6.5 averages 6 and 7, but the two middle values of the six remaining are 7 and 7.
n.1: The median is resistant to the outlier: the two middle values are both 7, so it stays at 7.
n.3: 41 / 7 = 5.9 is the outlier's share of the old mean, but the new mean is computed over 6 values: 12 - 7.17 = 4.8.

Data, Statistics & Variables.q: The mean price of 10 homes sold on a street last year was $310,000. If the one home that sold for $940,000 is removed, what is the mean price of the other 9 homes, in thousands of dollars? Enter the number only.

tr.310: the original mean, before the outlier is removed

Data, Statistics & Variables.w: Total of 10 homes = 10 x 310 = 3,100 thousand. Remove 940: 3,100 - 940 = 2,160 thousand. Mean of 9 = 2,160 / 9 = 240 thousand dollars.

Data, Statistics & Variables.q: Each of the 15 employees at a pharmacy receives a raise of $2.00 per hour. Before the raise, the hourly wages had a mean of $18.40, a median of $17.75, and a range of $9.50. Which describes the wages after the raise?
o: Mean $20.40, median $19.75, range $11.50
Mean $20.40, median $19.75, range $9.50
Mean $18.53, median $19.75, range $9.50
Mean $20.40, median $17.75, range $9.50
Data, Statistics & Variables.w: Adding the same amount to every value adds it to the mean and the median, but the gap between the highest and lowest wage does not change. Mean 18.40 + 2 = 20.40; median 17.75 + 2 = 19.75; range stays 9.50.

n.0: The range does not change: the highest and lowest wages both rise by $2.
n.2: Each employee gets $2, so the mean rises by $2, not by 2 / 15.
n.3: The middle wage also rises by $2, so the median becomes $19.75.

Data, Statistics & Variables.q: The annual salaries, in thousands of dollars, of the seven employees at a small clinic are 42, 45, 45, 48, 51, 54, and 160. How much greater is the mean salary than the median salary, in thousands of dollars? Round to the nearest tenth.

tr.18.6: mean minus the mode (45) instead of the median

Data, Statistics & Variables.w: Sum = 445, so mean = 445 / 7 = 63.57. Median = 4th value = 48. Difference = 63.57 - 48 = 15.57, about 15.6 thousand dollars.

Data, Statistics & Variables.q: In a data set of 20 hospital stays, the longest stay, 9 days, is entered by mistake as 90 days. Which statistic stays the same despite the error?
o: The range
The standard deviation
The median
The mean
Data, Statistics & Variables.w: The median depends on the middle values (the 10th and 11th of 20). Changing the largest value does not move the middle, so the median is unchanged.

n.0: The maximum changes from 9 to 90, so the range grows by 81.
n.1: The new extreme value lies far from the mean, which increases the spread.
n.3: The total rises by 81, so the mean rises by 81 / 20 = 4.05 days.

Data, Statistics & Variables.q: A large set of adult cholesterol levels is roughly symmetric and bell-shaped, with a mean of 190 mg/dL and a standard deviation of 20 mg/dL. Which statement is best supported?
o: About 68% of the levels fall between 170 and 210 mg/dL
About 95% of the levels fall between 170 and 210 mg/dL
About half of the levels are above 210 mg/dL
About 68% of the levels fall between 150 and 230 mg/dL
Data, Statistics & Variables.w: In a bell-shaped distribution, about 68% of values fall within 1 standard deviation of the mean: 190 - 20 = 170 to 190 + 20 = 210.

n.1: 170 to 210 is within 1 standard deviation, which holds about 68%, not 95%.
n.2: About half are above the mean of 190; only about 16% are above 210.
n.3: 150 to 230 is within 2 standard deviations, which holds about 95%, not 68%.

Data, Statistics & Variables.q: A clinic records each new patient's blood type (A, B, AB, or O) to help plan its blood supply. Which measure of center can be used to describe these data?
o: The median
The weighted mean
The mode
The mean
Data, Statistics & Variables.w: Blood type is categorical data with no numeric values or natural order, so the mode (the most common type) is the only usable measure of center.

n.0: A median needs values that can be put in a meaningful order; A, B, AB and O have none.
n.1: A weighted mean also needs numeric values to multiply by the weights.
n.3: A mean needs numeric values to add, and blood types are categories.

Data, Statistics & Variables.q: Data set A is 14, 18, 22, 26, 30. Data set B is 8, 21, 22, 23, 36. Which statement correctly compares the two data sets?
o: Same mean and median, but B has the greater range
Same mean and range, but the medians differ
Same mean and median, but A has the greater range
Same median, but B has the greater mean and range
