n.1: hemi- (half) is not hem/o (blood); the word says nothing about bleeding.
n.2: Paralysis of both legs is paraplegia; hemi- refers to one side, not both legs.
n.3: Paralysis of all four limbs is quadriplegia; quadri- means four.

Vocabulary & the Writing Process.q: After the patient's hip surgery, the doctor prescribed an anticoagulant to take for several weeks. Based on the prefix, what does an anticoagulant do?
o: Measures clotting time
Speeds up blood clotting
Works against blood clotting
Breaks down existing clots
Vocabulary & the Writing Process.w: anti- means against, and coagulant refers to clotting, so an anticoagulant works against the clotting of blood.

n.0: Nothing in the word refers to measuring; a measuring term would use -meter or a test name.
n.1: Speeding up clotting is the opposite of anti- (against).
n.3: Breaking down would be shown by -lysis (as in thrombolysis), not by anti-.

Vocabulary & the Writing Process.q: From across the room, the respiratory therapist noted that the patient's wheezing was audible without a stethoscope. Based on its root, what does audible mean?
o: Able to be spoken
Able to be seen
Able to be heard
Able to be felt
Vocabulary & the Writing Process.w: The root aud means hear, and -ible means able to be, so audible means able to be heard.

n.0: Speaking comes from voc (voice) or dict (say), not aud.
n.1: Able to be seen is visible, from the root vis/vid (see).
n.3: Able to be felt would come from sens/sent (feel), as in sensory.

Vocabulary & the Writing Process.q: Because the resident's bones have become fragile, staff use a mechanical lift to move him from his bed to a chair. Based on its root, what does fragile mean?
o: Easily carried
Easily broken
Easily pulled
Easily turned
Vocabulary & the Writing Process.w: The root frag (like fract) means break, so fragile means easily broken.

n.0: Carrying is the meaning of port (as in transport).
n.2: Pulling is the meaning of tract (as in traction).
n.3: Turning is the meaning of vert/vers (as in reverse), not frag.

Vocabulary & the Writing Process.q: The committee was persuaded by the epidemiologist's credible account of how the outbreak began in a school cafeteria. Based on its root, what does credible mean?
o: Able to be dictated
Able to be believed
Able to be visualized
Able to be recognized
Vocabulary & the Writing Process.w: The root cred means believe, and -ible means able to be, so credible means believable.

n.0: Saying is the meaning of dict, as in dictate.
n.2: Seeing is the meaning of vis/vid, as in visualize and visible.
n.3: Recognizing (knowing) is the meaning of cogn, as in recognize and cognitive.

Vocabulary & the Writing Process.q: A nursing instructor praised a student for showing empathy while talking with a grieving family. Based on its root, empathy is most closely related to which idea?
o: Feeling
Mind
Love
Knowledge
Vocabulary & the Writing Process.w: The root path means feeling (and also disease), so empathy is the ability to share or understand another person's feelings.

n.1: Mind is the meaning of psych (as in psychology).
n.2: Love is the meaning of phil (as in philanthropy).
n.3: Knowledge is the meaning of cogn (as in cognitive).

Vocabulary & the Writing Process.q: The physician told the unit clerk that she would dictate her notes on each patient after morning rounds. Based on its root, what will the physician do with her notes?
o: Look them over for errors
Say them aloud for recording
Send them on to another office
Write them out by hand
Vocabulary & the Writing Process.w: The root dict means say, so to dictate is to say words aloud for someone (or a device) to record.

n.0: Looking is the meaning of spec/spect (as in inspect).
n.2: Sending is the meaning of mit/mis (as in transmit).
n.3: Writing is the meaning of scrib/script (as in prescription).

Vocabulary & the Writing Process.q: After the patient's femur fracture, the orthopedic team placed his leg in traction until surgery could be scheduled. Based on its root, what does traction apply to the leg?
o: A twisting force that turns the limb
A steady pulling force on the limb
A brace that carries the limb's weight
A cut that opens the limb's tissue
Vocabulary & the Writing Process.w: The root tract means pull, so traction is a steady pulling force (used to align a broken bone).

n.0: Turning is the meaning of vert/vers, not tract.
n.2: Carrying is the meaning of port, not tract.
n.3: Cutting is the meaning of sect (as in dissect), not tract.

Vocabulary & the Writing Process.q: A student is grouping health-related words by their Greek and Latin roots. Which words contain a root meaning "write" or "record"? Select all that apply.
o: dictionary
spectator
biography
prescription
transportation
mammogram
Vocabulary & the Writing Process.w: script (prescription) means write, gram (mammogram) means write or record, and graph (biography) means write.

n.0: dict (dictionary) means say, not write.
n.1: spect (spectator) means look.
n.4: port (transportation) means carry.

Vocabulary & the Writing Process.q: As part of a rehabilitation assessment after a stroke, the occupational therapist tested the patient's manual dexterity. Based on its root, which body part does manual dexterity involve?
o: The feet
The voice
The hands
The eyes
Vocabulary & the Writing Process.w: The root man/manu means hand, so manual dexterity is skill in using the hands.

n.0: Foot is the meaning of ped/pod (as in podiatrist).
n.1: Voice is the meaning of voc/vok (as in vocal).
n.3: Eye or sight comes from vis/vid or ocul/o, not manu.

Vocabulary & the Writing Process.q: The hospital's quality committee reviewed mortality data from the past year to compare outcomes across its units. Based on its root, what do mortality data measure?
o: The number of diseases diagnosed
The number of deaths
The number of patients transferred
The number of births
Vocabulary & the Writing Process.w: The root mort means death, so mortality data measure deaths (for example, deaths per 1,000 patients).

n.0: Disease is the meaning of path (as in pathology).
n.2: Transfer relates to port (carry) or mit (send), not mort.
n.3: Births relate to natal (as in prenatal), not mort.

Vocabulary & the Writing Process.q: To track her walking program, the physical therapist asked an adult patient to wear a pedometer on her waistband all week. Based on its word parts and the context, what does a pedometer most likely measure?
o: Steps taken on foot
Body heat during a walk
Growth in a child's height
Heart rate during exercise
Vocabulary & the Writing Process.w: ped can mean foot or child, and the context (an adult's walking program) points to foot. A -meter measures, so a pedometer counts steps taken on foot.

n.1: Body heat would involve therm (heat), as in thermometer.
n.2: ped can mean child, but the patient is an adult tracking her walking, so foot is the meaning here.
n.3: Heart rate would involve cardi/o (heart), which is not in the word.

Vocabulary & the Writing Process.q: The pharmacist reassured the patient that the drug's side effects are reversible once the medication is stopped. Based on its root, what does reversible mean?
o: Able to be sent back
Able to be pulled back
Able to be turned back
Able to be built again
Vocabulary & the Writing Process.w: re- means back or again, the root vers means turn, and -ible means able to be, so reversible means able to be turned back (undone).

n.0: Sending is the meaning of mit/mis (as in remission or transmit), not vers.
n.1: Pulling is the meaning of tract (as in retract), not vers.
n.3: Building is the meaning of struct (as in reconstruct).

Vocabulary & the Writing Process.q: The patient's admission record lists chronic kidney disease among her conditions. Based on its root, what does the word chronic indicate about the disease?
o: It persists over a long time
It has been present since birth
It spreads from person to person
It started suddenly and is severe
Vocabulary & the Writing Process.w: The root chron means time, so a chronic condition is one that lasts a long time (the opposite of acute).

n.1: Present from birth is congenital (con- = with, gen = birth), not chronic.
n.2: Spreading between people describes a contagious disease; nothing in chron refers to spread.
n.3: A sudden, severe onset describes an acute condition; chron refers to time, meaning long-lasting.

Vocabulary & the Writing Process.q: After an ultrasound confirmed appendicitis, the surgeon scheduled an emergency appendectomy for that evening. Based on its suffix, what does appendectomy mean?
o: Surgical removal of the appendix
Visual examination of the appendix
Inflammation of the appendix
Surgical incision into the appendix
Vocabulary & the Writing Process.w: -ectomy means surgical removal (excision), so an appendectomy is the surgical removal of the appendix.

n.1: Visual examination is -scopy (as in colonoscopy).
n.2: Inflammation is -itis: appendicitis is the condition that led to the surgery, not the surgery itself.
n.3: Cutting into an organ without removing it is -otomy (incision), the look-alike suffix.

Vocabulary & the Writing Process.q: Read the sentence: "The therapist will gradually strengthen the weak muscle with careful exercises." Based on its suffix, which word is a noun that names a person?
o: careful
therapist
strengthen
gradually
Vocabulary & the Writing Process.w: The suffix -ist forms a noun meaning a person who does something (therapist, pharmacist, dentist).

n.0: -ful forms adjectives meaning full of (careful describes the exercises).
n.2: -en forms verbs meaning to make or become (strengthen = to make strong).
n.3: -ly usually forms adverbs (gradually describes how the action happens).

Vocabulary & the Writing Process.q: An X-ray of the patient's stiff knee showed arthritis, and the nurse practitioner discussed treatment options with him. Based on its suffix, what does arthritis mean?
o: Surgical repair of a joint
Pain in a joint
Inflammation of a joint
A tumor of a joint
Vocabulary & the Writing Process.w: arthr/o means joint and -itis means inflammation, so arthritis is inflammation of a joint.

n.0: Surgical repair is -plasty (arthroplasty), not -itis.
n.1: Joint pain is arthralgia; pain is -algia, not -itis.
n.3: A tumor or mass is -oma, not -itis.

Vocabulary & the Writing Process.q: Mrs. Patel's primary care provider referred her to Dr. Ruiz, a dermatologist, for a rash that would not heal. Based on the word's parts, what is Dr. Ruiz?
o: A tool for examining the skin
A specialist in blood conditions
The study of skin conditions
A specialist in skin conditions
Vocabulary & the Writing Process.w: dermat/o means skin and -logist means a specialist (one who studies), so a dermatologist is a skin specialist.

n.0: An instrument for viewing is -scope; a -logist is a person.
n.1: Blood is hem/o or hemat/o (as in hematologist), not dermat/o.
n.2: "The study of" is -logy (dermatology), a field, not a person; the -ist ending marks a person.

Vocabulary & the Writing Process.q: Before the next patient's procedure, the technician cleaned and tested the endoscope according to the hospital's infection-control policy. Based on its suffix, what is an endoscope?
o: A record of images from inside the body
A surgical cut made into the body
A procedure that views inside the body
An instrument for viewing inside the body
Vocabulary & the Writing Process.w: endo- means within and -scope means an instrument for viewing, so an endoscope is the instrument used to look inside the body.

n.0: A record or image is -gram; -scope is the viewing instrument.
n.1: A surgical cut is -otomy; nothing in endoscope refers to cutting.
n.2: The procedure is endoscopy; -scopy names the examination, while -scope names the instrument.

Vocabulary & the Writing Process.q: After his bowel surgery, Mr. Grant met with a wound-care nurse to learn how to care for his new colostomy at home. Based on the suffix, what is a colostomy?
o: A surgical incision made into the colon
Surgical removal of part of the colon
Surgical repair of a damaged colon
A surgical opening made for the colon
Vocabulary & the Writing Process.w: -ostomy means a surgically created opening (a new mouth), so a colostomy is an opening that lets the colon empty through the abdominal wall.

n.0: A cut into an organ is -otomy (colotomy); -ostomy names a created opening, not a simple incision.
n.1: Removal is -ectomy (colectomy).
n.2: Repair is -plasty.

Vocabulary & the Writing Process.q: A patient-education leaflet uses each of the words below. Based on their suffixes, which of the words are adjectives? Select all that apply.
o: rapidly
donor
treatable
painful
nervous
sterilize
Vocabulary & the Writing Process.w: -ful (full of), -able (able to be) and -ous (having, full of) form adjectives: painful, treatable, nervous.

n.0: -ly added to an adjective forms an adverb (rapidly).
n.1: -or forms a noun naming a person (donor = one who gives).
n.5: -ize forms verbs meaning to make (sterilize = to make sterile).

Vocabulary & the Writing Process.q: During chemotherapy, a patient's blood test revealed leukopenia, so the nurse reviewed infection precautions with him. Based on its word parts, what does leukopenia mean?
o: A deficiency of white blood cells
A cancer of the white blood cells
An excess of white blood cells
A deficiency of red blood cells
Vocabulary & the Writing Process.w: leuk/o means white and -penia means deficiency, so leukopenia is a shortage of white blood cells (which explains the infection precautions).

n.1: Cancer would be shown by carcin/o or -oma (or -emia in leukemia, a blood condition); -penia means deficiency.
n.2: An excess would use hyper- or -cytosis; -penia means deficiency.
n.3: Red is erythr/o; leuk/o means white.

Vocabulary & the Writing Process.q: A chest X-ray and an echocardiogram both showed cardiomegaly in a patient with long-term high blood pressure. Based on its word parts, what does cardiomegaly mean?
o: Hardening of the heart
Narrowing of the heart valves
Enlargement of the heart
Softening of the heart
Vocabulary & the Writing Process.w: cardi/o means heart and -megaly means enlargement, so cardiomegaly is an enlarged heart.

n.0: Hardening is -sclerosis.
n.1: Narrowing is -stenosis (as in aortic stenosis).
n.3: Softening is -malacia.

Vocabulary & the Writing Process.q: Read the sentence: "Before each procedure, staff must ______ every instrument that will touch the patient." Based on its suffix, which word correctly completes the sentence?
o: sterile
sterilize
sterility
sterilely
Vocabulary & the Writing Process.w: The blank follows the helping verb must, so it needs a verb. The suffix -ize forms verbs meaning to make, so sterilize (to make sterile) fits.

n.0: Sterile is an adjective; "must sterile every instrument" has no verb.
n.2: -ity forms a noun (the state of being sterile), which cannot follow must.
n.3: -ly forms an adverb, which describes a verb rather than serving as one.

Vocabulary & the Writing Process.q: The lab returned the patient's sample with a note that hemolysis had occurred during collection, so the blood had to be drawn again. Based on its word parts, what does hemolysis mean?
o: Bursting forth of blood
Breakdown of blood cells
Abnormal clotting of blood
Stopping of blood flow
Vocabulary & the Writing Process.w: hem/o means blood and -lysis means breakdown or destruction, so hemolysis is the breakdown of (red) blood cells.

n.0: Bursting forth of blood (bleeding) is hemorrhage; -rrhage is the suffix.
n.2: A clot is thromb/o (thrombosis); -lysis means breakdown, the opposite of forming a clot.
n.3: Stopping blood flow is hemostasis; -stasis means stopping.

Vocabulary & the Writing Process.q: After the test, the technician handed the cardiologist a printed tracing that recorded the electrical activity of the patient's heart. Based on its suffix, what is this printed tracing called?
o: Electrocardiograph
Electrocardiography
Electrocardiology
Electrocardiogram
Vocabulary & the Writing Process.w: Step 1: the item is the record itself, not the process or the machine. Step 2: -gram means a record, so the printed tracing is an electrocardiogram.

n.0: -graph names the instrument that does the recording, not its output.
n.1: -graphy names the process of recording, not the printed record.
n.2: -logy means the study of, a field of knowledge, not a record.

Vocabulary & the Writing Process.q: After routine blood work showed a decline in organ function, the patient's primary care provider referred him to a nephrologist. Based on its root, which organs does a nephrologist specialize in?
o: The liver
The nerves
The kidneys
The lungs
Vocabulary & the Writing Process.w: nephr/o means kidney and -logist means specialist, so a nephrologist specializes in the kidneys.

n.0: The liver is hepat/o (hepatologist).
n.1: Nerves are neur/o, the look-alike root (neurologist).
n.3: The lungs are pneum/o or pulmon/o (pulmonologist).

Vocabulary & the Writing Process.q: The provider explained to an older patient that her bone pain was caused by osteomalacia linked to low vitamin D levels. Based on its word parts, what does osteomalacia mean?
o: Inflammation of the bones
Softening of the bones
Hardening of the bones
Softening of the cartilage
Vocabulary & the Writing Process.w: oste/o means bone and -malacia means softening, so osteomalacia is softening of the bones.

n.0: Inflammation is -itis (osteitis).
n.2: Hardening is -sclerosis, not -malacia.
n.3: Cartilage is chondr/o (chondromalacia); oste/o means bone.

Vocabulary & the Writing Process.q: While assessing a child with a severe asthma attack, the nurse noticed cyanosis around the lips and fingertips. Based on its word parts, what does cyanosis describe?
o: A reddish discoloration
A bluish discoloration
A whitish discoloration
A blackish discoloration
Vocabulary & the Writing Process.w: cyan/o means blue and -osis means an abnormal condition, so cyanosis is a bluish discoloration of the skin (a sign of low oxygen).

n.0: Red is erythr/o.
n.2: White is leuk/o.
n.3: Black is melan/o.

Vocabulary & the Writing Process.q: In the outpatient lab, a phlebotomist called the next patient's name and prepared the collection tubes for his blood test. Based on its root, which structures does a phlebotomist work with?
o: Lymph nodes
Nerves
Veins
Arteries
Vocabulary & the Writing Process.w: phleb/o means vein, -tomy means cutting into (incision), and -ist means a person, so a phlebotomist is trained to puncture veins to draw blood.

n.0: Lymph nodes have their own root (lymph/o), not phleb/o.
n.1: Nerves are neur/o.
n.3: Arteries are arteri/o; phleb/o means vein.

Vocabulary & the Writing Process.q: After a long flight, a patient developed pain and redness in her calf, and an ultrasound confirmed thrombophlebitis. Using all of its word parts, what does thrombophlebitis mean?
o: Vein hardening caused by a blood clot
Surgical removal of a clot in a vein
Vein inflammation with a blood clot
Artery inflammation with a blood clot
Vocabulary & the Writing Process.w: Step 1: thromb/o means clot and phleb/o means vein. Step 2: -itis means inflammation. Together: inflammation of a vein associated with a blood clot.

n.0: Hardening is -sclerosis; -itis means inflammation.
n.1: Removal is -ectomy (thrombectomy); -itis means inflammation.
n.3: Artery is arteri/o; phleb/o means vein.

Vocabulary & the Writing Process.q: A soccer player was kicked in the thigh, and by the next day a firm, painful hematoma had formed under the skin. Based on its word parts, what is a hematoma?
o: A shortage of blood cells
A swelling or mass of blood
An inflamed blood vessel
A tumor of the liver
Vocabulary & the Writing Process.w: hemat/o means blood and -oma means a tumor or mass, so a hematoma is a localized mass (swelling) of blood, such as a deep bruise.

n.0: A shortage of cells would use -penia (or anemia, a blood condition); -oma means a mass.
n.2: Inflammation of a vessel would use vas/o or angi/o with -itis.
n.3: Liver is hepat/o, the look-alike root; hemat/o means blood.

Vocabulary & the Writing Process.q: A student is reviewing a list of terms from a cardiac unit's orientation packet. Based on their word parts, which terms refer to the heart? Select all that apply.
o: pericarditis
hepatomegaly
carcinoma
encephalitis
tachycardia
cardiomegaly
Vocabulary & the Writing Process.w: All three contain cardi/o (heart): cardiomegaly (enlarged heart), pericarditis (inflammation of the sac around the heart) and tachycardia (fast heart rate).

n.1: hepat/o means liver; hepatomegaly is an enlarged liver.
n.2: carcin/o means cancer, not heart, despite the similar first letters.
n.3: encephal/o means brain; encephalitis is inflammation of the brain.

Vocabulary & the Writing Process.q: A mother brings her toddler to the clinic with a mild cold, a low fever, and persistent rhinorrhea. Based on its word parts, what is rhinorrhea?
o: Inflammation of the nose
A discharge from the nose
Bleeding from the nose
Surgical repair of the nose
Vocabulary & the Writing Process.w: rhin/o means nose and -rrhea means flow or discharge, so rhinorrhea is a runny nose.

n.0: Inflammation of the nose is rhinitis (-itis).
n.2: Bleeding (bursting forth) is -rrhage or -rrhagia, the look-alike suffix.
n.3: Surgical repair is -plasty (rhinoplasty).

Vocabulary & the Writing Process.q: A complete blood count reports the number of erythrocytes in a sample, along with other values. Based on its word parts, what are erythrocytes?
o: Clot-forming cells
White blood cells
Skin pigment cells
Red blood cells
Vocabulary & the Writing Process.w: erythr/o means red and -cyte means cell, so erythrocytes are red blood cells.

n.0: Clot-forming cells are thrombocytes (thromb/o = clot).
n.1: White blood cells are leukocytes (leuk/o = white).
n.2: Pigment cells are melanocytes (melan/o = black).

Vocabulary & the Writing Process.q: After a fall from a ladder, a construction worker had a CT scan that ruled out intracranial bleeding. Based on its word parts, where would intracranial bleeding occur?
o: Between the skull bones
Around the outer skull
Below the skull
Inside the skull
Vocabulary & the Writing Process.w: intra- means within and crani/o means skull, so intracranial means inside the skull.

n.0: Between is inter-, the look-alike prefix.
n.1: Around is peri- or circum-.
n.2: Below is sub- or hypo-.

Vocabulary & the Writing Process.q: A tall, thin teenager arrived at the emergency department short of breath, and a chest X-ray confirmed a pneumothorax. Based on its word parts, what is a pneumothorax?
o: Pain in the chest wall
Inflammation of a lung
Air in the chest cavity
A surgical cut into the chest
Vocabulary & the Writing Process.w: pneum/o means air or lung and thorac/o means chest, so a pneumothorax is air in the chest cavity (around the lung).

n.0: Pain would need a pain suffix such as -algia or -dynia.
n.1: Inflammation would need -itis (as in pneumonitis).
n.3: A surgical cut would need -otomy (thoracotomy).

Vocabulary & the Writing Process.q: A patient with repeated attacks of pain from gallstones is scheduled for a cholecystectomy next week. Using all of its word parts, what will the surgeon do?
o: Examine the gallbladder
Remove the gallbladder
Remove the urinary bladder
Cut into the gallbladder
Vocabulary & the Writing Process.w: Step 1: chol/e means bile and cyst/o means bladder or sac, so cholecyst is the bile sac (gallbladder). Step 2: -ectomy means surgical removal. A cholecystectomy removes the gallbladder.

n.0: Visual examination is -scopy, not -ectomy.
n.2: cyst/o alone can mean the urinary bladder, but chol/e (bile) makes this the gallbladder.
n.3: Cutting into an organ is -otomy, not -ectomy.

Vocabulary & the Writing Process.q: Because the medication is contraindicated during pregnancy, the pharmacist called the provider to suggest a different drug for the patient. Based on its prefix and the context, what does contraindicated mean?
o: Advised before other treatment
Advised again after a review
Advised together with another drug
Advised against for a patient
Vocabulary & the Writing Process.w: contra- means against, and the context (the pharmacist seeks a different drug) confirms it: a contraindicated drug is one advised against for that patient or situation.

n.0: Before is ante- or pre-, not contra-.
n.1: Again is re-, not contra-.
n.2: Together with is co-, com- or con-, not contra-; the pharmacist is replacing the drug, not adding one.

Vocabulary & the Writing Process.q: A warning label on a can of cleaning solvent reads, "Inflammable: store away from heat, sparks, and open flames." Based on the context, what does inflammable mean?
o: Safe to store near heat
Unable to catch fire
Harmful if breathed in
Easily set on fire
Vocabulary & the Writing Process.w: Here in- does not mean not: inflammable means the same as flammable. The context (keep it away from heat, sparks and flames) confirms that the product catches fire easily.

n.0: This also reads in- as "not," which contradicts the instruction to store it away from heat.
n.1: This reads in- as "not," but the warning to keep the can away from flames shows it can catch fire.
n.2: The label's warning is about fire, and nothing in the word parts refers to breathing.

Vocabulary & the Writing Process.q: Dr. Shah works in the pediatric unit, where her patients range from newborns to teenagers. Based on the context, what does the word part ped mean in pediatric?
o: Foot
Child
Birth
Bone
Vocabulary & the Writing Process.w: ped can mean foot (pedal) or child (pediatric). The context (patients from newborns to teenagers) shows that here it means child.

n.0: ped can mean foot, as in pedal, but a unit serving newborns to teenagers is about children.
n.2: Birth is natal (as in prenatal), not ped.
n.3: Bone is oste/o, not ped.

Vocabulary & the Writing Process.q: In a retrospective study, researchers reviewed ten years of patient records to see whether earlier screening had changed outcomes. Based on its word parts and the context, what does retrospective mean?
o: Looking back at past events
Looking across several groups
Looking ahead to future events
Looking within one person
Vocabulary & the Writing Process.w: retro- means backward and spect means look, so retrospective means looking back. The context (reviewing ten years of past records) confirms it.

n.1: Across is trans-, not retro-.
n.2: Looking ahead is the meaning of pro- or pre- words such as prospective; retro- means backward.
n.3: Within is intra- or endo-, not retro-.

Vocabulary & the Writing Process.q: Before the clinical trial began, researchers sorted the volunteers into groups so that each group was homogeneous in age. Based on its prefix, what does homogeneous mean here?
o: Different throughout
Many in number
Divided into halves
Similar throughout
Vocabulary & the Writing Process.w: homo-/homeo- means same or similar, so a group homogeneous in age is made of people of similar ages.

n.0: Different is hetero- (heterogeneous), the opposite prefix.
n.1: Many is multi- or poly-, not homo-.
n.2: Half is hemi- or semi-, not homo-.

Vocabulary & the Writing Process.q: During a dressing change, the nurse documented a malodorous discharge from the patient's wound and notified the provider. Based on its prefix, what does malodorous mean?
o: Having no smell
Having a faint smell
Having a bad smell
Having a pleasant smell
Vocabulary & the Writing Process.w: mal- means bad, and odor means smell, so malodorous means having a bad smell.

n.0: No smell would use a- or an- (without), not mal-.
n.1: Faint (less than normal) would match hypo-, not mal-.
n.3: A pleasant smell is the opposite of mal- (bad); good would be eu- or bene.

Vocabulary & the Writing Process.q: A medical terminology instructor asks students to work out the meaning of in- from context. In which sentence does the prefix in- mean "not"?
o: The tumor was found to be inoperable.
The nurse will inject the vaccine into the upper arm.
Patients should inhale slowly through the mouth.
Insert the catheter gently into the opening.
Vocabulary & the Writing Process.w: in- can mean not or into. In inoperable it means not: the tumor is not able to be operated on.

n.1: In inject, in- means into: to throw (ject) medicine into the body.
n.2: In inhale, in- means into: to breathe in.
n.3: In insert, in- means into: to put something into an opening.

Vocabulary & the Writing Process.q: After a fall on an icy sidewalk, the patient's X-ray report noted bilateral wrist fractures. Based on its prefix, what does bilateral mean in this report?
o: Affecting the area between
Affecting both sides
Affecting one side
Affecting all four limbs
Vocabulary & the Writing Process.w: bi- means two, and lateral refers to sides, so bilateral means affecting both sides (both wrists).

n.0: Between is inter-, not bi-.
n.2: One side is unilateral; uni- means one.
n.3: Four is quadri- or tetra-; bi- means two.

Vocabulary & the Writing Process.q: During the resident's quarterly medication review, the geriatric care team flagged polypharmacy as a risk for falls. Based on its word parts, what is polypharmacy?
o: Use of several pharmacies to fill orders
Use of a drug that affects many organs
Use of many medications at the same time
Use of one medication at too high a dose
Vocabulary & the Writing Process.w: poly- means many and pharmac/o refers to drugs, so polypharmacy is the use of many medications at the same time, which raises the risk of side effects, drug interactions and falls in older adults.

n.0: Here pharmacy refers to drugs (pharmac/o), not to the stores that fill prescriptions; polypharmacy is about how many medications a person takes.
n.1: poly- (many) applies to the drugs themselves; nothing in the word refers to organs or body systems.
n.3: poly- means many, so the word refers to the number of drugs, not to one drug at too high a dose (one is mono- or uni-).

Vocabulary & the Writing Process.q: In anatomy lab, each pair of students began the dissection of a preserved frog, following the steps in the lab manual. Based on all of its word parts, what does dissection mean?
o: To cut apart a specimen for study
The act of cutting apart for study
The study of how living things work
A tool used to cut apart a specimen
Vocabulary & the Writing Process.w: Step 1: dis- means apart and sect means cut. Step 2: -tion forms a noun naming an act or process. Dissection is the act of cutting something apart (for study).

n.0: This defines the verb dissect; the -tion suffix makes dissection a noun.
n.2: The study of living things is biology (bio + -logy), and the word has no part meaning study.
n.3: -tion names an act or process, not a tool (the tool is a scalpel).

Vocabulary & the Writing Process.q: Instead of taking pills, the patient now uses a transdermal patch, changed every three days, to manage her chronic pain. Based on its word parts, how does the patch deliver medication?
o: Into a vein
Into a muscle
Through the skin
Under the tongue
Vocabulary & the Writing Process.w: trans- means across or through and derm/o means skin, so a transdermal patch delivers medication through the skin.

n.0: Into a vein is intravenous (ven/o = vein).
n.1: Into a muscle is intramuscular (my/o, muscul = muscle).
n.3: Under the tongue is sublingual (sub- = under, lingu/o = tongue).

Vocabulary & the Writing Process.q: In a medication trial, some volunteers reported euphoria, feeling unusually cheerful, while others reported dysphoria. Based on the prefix, what did the second group most likely feel?
o: An absence of mood
A sense of disbelief
Unease or a low mood
A calm, normal mood
Vocabulary & the Writing Process.w: Step 1: euphoria (eu- = good) is a good feeling. Step 2: dys- means bad or difficult, so dysphoria is a bad feeling: unease or low mood.

n.0: Absence is a- or an- (without), not dys-.
n.1: This confuses dys- (bad) with the look-alike dis- (apart, not), as in disbelief.
n.3: Good or normal is eu-, the prefix in euphoria; dys- means bad.
